findings.title: Enrollment-token admin routes are public (anyone can mint tokens, list tokens)
findings.evidence: src/app.ts:194-206 global gate whitelists `'/enroll/'` in `publicPrefixes` ("Device enrollment") and `if (publicPrefixes.some(p => path.startsWith(p))) return next();`. The admin routes live under that prefix with no per-route auth: app.ts:629 `app.post('/api/enroll/tokens', (req,res)=>{...enrollmentStore.createToken(...)`, :643 `app.get('/api/enroll/tokens'` (returns every active token value), :654 `app.delete('/api/enroll/tokens/:id'`.
findings.scenario: `curl -X POST https://proxymdm.../api/enroll/tokens -d '{"maxUses":1000,"expiresInHours":8760}'` returns a valid token; `POST /api/enroll/device` with it returns a deviceId + 30-day sessionToken (schema.ts:682). Attacker now holds a fleet-trusted device identity (see SS-03 for what that buys). `GET /api/enroll/tokens` also leaks tokens the admin created for real devices (race to use them) and `DELETE` lets anyone revoke them (DoS on provisioning).
findings.fix: split public from admin: keep only `POST /enroll/device` public (`publicExact = ['/enroll/device']`) and put `authMiddleware` on `/enroll/tokens*`. Add a rate limit on `/api/enroll/device` (tokens are 8 chars of a 32-letter alphabet = 40 bits, no limiter at app.ts:669).

findings.title: WebRTC signaling `/ws` has no authentication: anyone can hijack a remote-desktop session
findings.evidence: src/signaling.ts:171-186 upgrade handler accepts `/ws` with no token/origin check; `join` (signaling.ts:~262) takes `deviceId` and `role` straight from the message: `const { deviceId, role } = message;`, and "If role already taken, evict the stale peer": `existingPeer.ws.close(1000,'Replaced by new connection')`. Offers/answers/ICE are blindly forwarded to the other role (signaling.ts:~305). `validateSessionToken` is imported in app.ts only; signaling.ts never touches sessions.
findings.scenario: attacker knows a deviceId (leaks via SS-05, or any device-facing URL). They connect to `wss://host/ws`, send `{"type":"join","deviceId":X,"role":"controller"}`. The admin's controller socket is evicted; when the Android app joins for START_REMOTE it gets `peer-joined` and sends its SDP offer to the attacker, who answers and receives the screen and can send input over the data channel. Alternatively join as `role:"device"` to evict the real device and feed a fake stream to the admin, or just spam join to kill every session.
findings.fix: require auth on upgrade: controllers must present the admin JWT (`?token=`/subprotocol), devices their session token validated with `validateSessionToken(db, token, deviceId)` (also check `expires_at`); bind the role to the credential type and reject join when the deviceId does not match the token's device. Do not evict an authenticated peer from an unauthenticated one. Check the `Origin` header for browser (controller) connections.

findings.title: Relay viewer accepts ANY device session token (no device binding, no expiry): shell/files/desktop on every connected desktop agent
findings.evidence: src/relay.ts:505-519: JWT verify, else "Also accept session tokens (for simpler auth)": `SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE token = ?` then `userId = 'agent-session'`; `deviceId` comes from the URL (`params.get('deviceId')`, relay.ts:116) and is never compared to `session.device_id`; `expires_at` is not checked (compare validateSessionToken). Any message is then forwarded to the agent with only the channel rewritten (relay.ts:549-567), including TERMINAL_OPEN-side data, FILE_DELETE_REQ, DESKTOP_INPUT, regardless of the `session=` type requested.
findings.scenario: SS-01 (or SS-04) gives an attacker a session token in two requests. They open `wss://host/relay?deviceId=<victim>&session=terminal&token=<their token>` and get an interactive shell on a victim desktop agent (agent runs shell via TERMINAL_OPEN payload `shell:null`, relay.ts:605). The same works with a legitimately enrolled but compromised/low-value Android device. Even an expired (30-day) token keeps working forever here.
findings.fix: viewers must be admin JWTs only (drop the session-token branch; agents authenticate through AUTH_REQUEST). If kept, require `session.device_id === deviceId` and `expires_at > now`. Restrict forwarded message types per `sessionType` (a `desktop` channel should not be able to send TERMINAL_*/FILE_* frames). Also move the token out of the URL (nginx logs it), e.g. first-message auth like the agent path.

findings.title: Anyone can self-enroll through the public pairing flow (no admin involved) and get a valid session token
findings.evidence: app.ts:372-450: `/api/pair/initiate` (any caller, 10/min/IP) creates a pairing session; `/api/pair/complete` (any caller) with the code returns `sessionToken` and `deviceId` (app.ts:442-447), and `pairingStore.completeSession` auto-enrolls the device into the MDM (pairingStore.ts:~178 `deviceStore.enrollDevice(...)`) and writes a 30-day session. `/api/pair/status/:deviceId` is public and also returns the sessionToken (app.ts:480-483). Code is `Math.floor(100000 + Math.random()*900000)` (pairingStore.ts:82), non-crypto RNG, 6 digits.
findings.scenario: attacker calls initiate, takes the returned code, calls complete: a new device record appears in the admin fleet list with a working sessionToken. Used with SS-03 for relay access; also pollutes the fleet, can POST telemetry/events, and appears as a trusted device. Also, guessing a victim's live 6-digit code (15 tries/min/IP, 5 min window, rotating IPs) lets the attacker steal the pairing and the legitimate device's session token.
findings.fix: gate pairing on an admin-issued secret (e.g. require a valid enrollment token in `/pair/initiate`, or let the admin UI own the "complete" step with JWT). Use `crypto.randomInt`. Auto-enrolled devices should start as `pending approval`.

findings.title: Admin event WebSocket `/admin` is unauthenticated
findings.evidence: signaling.ts:~176-179 `else if (pathname === '/admin') { adminWss.handleUpgrade(...)`; `adminWss.on('connection', (ws)=>{ ... adminConnections.set(ws, subscription)` with no check. Events broadcast include deviceId, eventType, severity, data (`broadcastEventToAdmins`, signaling.ts:~58).
findings.scenario: `wscat -c wss://host/admin` streams every device event (online/offline, battery, command completed/failed with commandId, enrollment, device names/models): live fleet intel and the deviceId list needed for SS-02 and SS-06.
findings.fix: authenticate the upgrade with the admin JWT (query token or first message) and close otherwise.

findings.title: Device-facing endpoints accept requests with NO token ("backward compat"), so devices are never actually authenticated
findings.evidence: app.ts:228-233: `if (!sessionToken) { return next(); // Allow without token for backward compat during migration }`. Covers POST heartbeat/telemetry/apps/events and GET `/commands/pending`, `/app-updates`, `/policy`. Android client sends none: CommandApiClient.kt:56 `httpClient.get("$baseUrl/api/devices/$deviceId/commands/pending")` with no header (no `X-Session-Token`/Authorization anywhere in app/ per grep).
findings.scenario: knowing only a deviceId (64-bit random; leaks via SS-05): `GET /api/devices/<id>/commands/pending` returns the queued commands including payloads (install URLs, SEND_MESSAGE text, SET_PASSWORD payloads); `GET /api/devices/<id>/policy` returns the full policy (check for kiosk_exit_password in schema.ts:45); `POST .../apps` overwrites the device's app inventory; `POST .../events` injects fake critical events into the admin console; `POST .../heartbeat` keeps a dead/stolen device "online" and queues SYNC_APPS. A device with a valid token is only checked against its own id, so A cannot act as B, but the no-token path makes that moot.
findings.fix: make the token mandatory (`return res.status(401)`), make the Android client send `X-Session-Token` on every call, and delete `deviceFacingPaths`' substring matching (`path.includes(...)`, app.ts:216-222) in favour of explicit method+regex routes.
findings.mitigation: when a token IS sent it is validated against the path deviceId (validateSessionToken, app.ts:244) and expiry is enforced; device cannot call admin routes (those fall to `authMiddleware`).

findings.title: Default `admin`/`admin` credential accepted when no hash is configured; prod doc never sets one
findings.evidence: auth.ts:80-89: `if (!passwordHash) { ... Accepting default password "admin" ... if (password !== 'admin')`. `mustChangePassword` is only a response flag; the issued JWT is fully privileged (auth.ts:105). docs/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md PM2 env sets only NODE_ENV and PORT (no ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH, no JWT_SECRET; grep for those names in the doc returns nothing).
findings.scenario: an operator following the guide gets an internet-facing server where `admin/admin` yields a JWT able to RUN_SHELL/WIPE/INSTALL_APK across the fleet. Separately: index.ts:9-13 `process.exit(1)` in production when JWT_SECRET is unset, so the documented deployment crash-loops under PM2 until the operator figures out the variable (reliability).
findings.fix: in production refuse to start (or refuse login) without ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH/stored hash; generate a one-time random bootstrap password printed to the log. Enforce mustChangePassword server-side (issue a restricted-scope JWT that only permits `PUT /auth/password`). Add JWT_SECRET/ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH to the doc's ecosystem file.

findings.title: Login rate limit is keyed on the proxy IP in the documented topology (shared bucket = lockout of the real admin)
findings.evidence: app.ts:172-180 `max: 5` per 15 min, default key = `req.ip`; app.ts:49 `app.set('trust proxy', process.env.TRUST_PROXY || 'loopback')`; doc forwards from Nginx Proxy Manager to a LAN IP (`proxy_pass http://<SERVER_IP>:7899`), so the TCP peer is not loopback and X-Forwarded-For is ignored.
findings.scenario: all clients share one counter. An attacker sends 5 bad logins and the admin cannot log in for 15 min (repeatable). Conversely 5 attempts per window across the world is the only brute-force defence, and failed logins are not logged/audited (auth.ts has no audit calls).
findings.fix: document/set `TRUST_PROXY` to the proxy's address in the deployment guide; key by username+IP; audit failed and successful logins (`admin.login` action type already exists in auditStore.ts:48 region but is never emitted).

findings.title: Admin JWT: 24h, no revocation, no logout, password change does not invalidate; token also sent in WS URL
findings.evidence: auth.ts:105 `jwt.sign({ username }, getJwtSecret(), { expiresIn: '24h' })`; no logout route (grep "logout" in server/src: only an audit-action enum name, never emitted); changePasswordHandler (auth.ts:~140) just stores the new hash. relay.ts:122 takes `token` from the query string. Secret comes from `JWT_SECRET` or a random per-boot value (auth.ts:26) - acceptable, but in non-production the server runs happily with it (restart invalidates sessions).
findings.scenario: a stolen JWT (proxy access log containing the relay URL, shared browser) stays valid up to 24h even after the admin changes the password.
findings.fix: add `tokenVersion`/`iat` check against a `passwordChangedAt` setting in authMiddleware; shorten expiry or add refresh; avoid query-string tokens.

findings.title: APK upload: no APK validation, path traversal via `packageName`, public unauthenticated download, no integrity data to the device
findings.evidence: app.ts:36-44 multer `fileFilter` only checks `file.originalname.endsWith('.apk')`; app.ts:1555-1557 `const filename = \`apks/${packageName}-${timestamp}.apk\`` with `packageName` taken raw from the form body, then `LocalStorageProvider.save` does `path.join(this.baseDir, filename)` and `writeFile` with no containment check (storageProvider.ts:55-66); delete uses the same join (:79). `app.use('/api/uploads', express.static(uploadsDir))` is registered before auth (app.ts:74) and `/uploads/` is also whitelisted (app.ts:200). INSTALL_APK payload has only url/packageName/versionName (app.ts:1688-1693), no sha256 or signature, and the Android client has no checksum verification (grep for sha256/checksum in app/src/main finds nothing).
findings.scenario: (a) admin-or-stolen-JWT upload with `packageName=../../../../etc/cron.d/x` writes a file outside uploads (the `.apk` suffix is forced, limiting but not removing impact, e.g. overwriting `dist/*.apk`-named targets or filling disk); same concern for `version` in agent-binary upload: `android-remote-agent-${os}-${arch}-v${version}${ext}` (agentBinaryStore.ts:~71) with unsanitized `version`. (b) Anyone who guesses/sees the URL `/api/uploads/apks/<pkg>-<ms-timestamp>.apk` can download your private APKs (no auth); timestamps are guessable. (c) The device installs whatever the URL returns; with an HTTP LAN base URL (doc allows `http://` patterns) a MITM can swap the APK.
findings.fix: validate `packageName` with `/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)+$/`, and after join assert `path.resolve(full).startsWith(baseDir + sep)`; same for agent `version` (`/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`). Check ZIP magic `PK\x03\x04` and parse the manifest to confirm packageName/versionCode. Put `sha256` in the INSTALL_APK payload and verify on device before `PackageInstaller`. Serve APKs through an authenticated route (device session token) or signed, expiring URLs.

findings.title: Command/privileged-action audit gaps
findings.evidence: auditStore.log appears in only the routes listed by action (app.deleted, app.deployed, command.queued only in package install, command.batch_queued, file.*, group.*, policy.*, event.acknowledged, app.uploaded/updated). `POST /api/commands` (app.ts:1053) and `POST /api/devices/:id/commands` (app.ts:1141), the paths that queue WIPE, REBOOT, RUN_SHELL, SET_PASSWORD, LOST_MODE, have no audit call. Also unaudited: login/failed login, password change, enrollment-token create/revoke, device unenroll (DELETE /devices/:id), settings, agent binary/installer upload. `actorId` on event acknowledge is client-supplied (`acknowledgedBy`, app.ts:~2535).
findings.scenario: after a fleet wipe or shell command there is no record of who queued it or from where.
findings.fix: add `auditStore.log({actorType:'admin', actorId: (req.user as any).username, ip: req.ip, ...})` in those handlers; take actor from `req.user`, never from the body.

findings.title: Telemetry body can override the target deviceId (cross-device write)
findings.evidence: app.ts:1330-1333 `const input: TelemetryInput = { deviceId: id, ...req.body };` and the schema is `.passthrough()` (app.ts:171) so `deviceId` in the body is kept and wins; `telemetryStore.updateTelemetry` uses `input.deviceId` (telemetryStore.ts:183,205).
findings.scenario: device A (valid token for A, or tokenless per SS-06) POSTs to `/api/devices/A/telemetry` with `{"deviceId":"B","battery_level":1}` and writes B's telemetry, raising false battery-critical events for B (events use `id`, telemetry uses B).
findings.fix: `{ ...req.body, deviceId: id }` (spread order) and drop `.passthrough()` or whitelist keys.

findings.title: Device command acknowledge and file-transfer callbacks cannot authenticate (functional break of the command loop)
findings.evidence: gate allows device-facing PATCH only if the path includes `/heartbeat|/telemetry|/apps|/commands/pending|/events` (app.ts:216-222). The Android ack goes to `PATCH /api/devices/$deviceId/commands/$commandId` (CommandApiClient.kt:133), which matches none, so it falls through to `authMiddleware` (JWT) and returns 401 for the device. Same for `PATCH /api/files/:id` "(device callback)" (app.ts:2696), a non-`/devices/` path.
findings.scenario: by code reading, commands are never acknowledged as completed/failed (no command-completed events, retries/repeat delivery depending on getPendingCommands semantics). Verify on a live device before relying on this; if acks do succeed there is another bypass I did not find.
findings.fix: add explicit device-auth route for `PATCH /devices/:id/commands/:cmdId` (verify the command belongs to :id, `commandStore.getCommand(cmdId).deviceId === id`; currently the handler ignores `:id` entirely, so device A could ack/fail device B's commands once auth exists) and for file callbacks.

findings.title: Host-header-derived URLs embedded in installers and API responses
findings.evidence: getBaseUrl falls back to `req.get('host')` when BASE_URL is unset (app.ts:~300-320); used for the installer trailer `JSON.stringify({ serverUrl, enrollToken })` (app.ts:~965) and `/api/agent/latest` url (app.ts:~795 uses `req.get('host')` directly).
findings.scenario: a request with a forged Host header while holding a valid enrollment token yields an installer that enrolls victims to the attacker's server; an in-path attacker can do the same. The installer and agent binaries carry no signature (sha256 comes from the same server).
findings.fix: require BASE_URL in production; ignore Host. Sign agent binaries/installers and have the agent verify.

findings.title: Minor config notes
findings.evidence:
• CORS reflects any RFC1918 / localhost origin with `credentials: true` (app.ts:77-105); harmless today because auth is Bearer, but any LAN web page can call the API with a stolen token; production-only origins require editing source (doc section 3) instead of `CORS_ORIGIN`.
• CSP `connectSrc: ["'self'", "ws:", "wss:"]` allows WebSocket to any host (app.ts:64); only matters for the API origin.
• Pre-auth relay agent socket buffers unbounded bytes: `readBuffer = Buffer.concat([readBuffer, data])` before AUTH (relay.ts:176) and the auth timeout is cleared as soon as an AUTH_REQUEST header arrives (relay.ts:192), so a peer that sends a partial header can hold memory/sockets; no per-IP limits on WS upgrades.
• Hard-coded `data/installers`, `agent-binaries`, `uploads` are inside the server tree; confirm they are gitignored (git check-ignore returned nothing for them; no binaries are tracked, `uploads/` is empty).

---

findings.title: Device command acknowledgements are rejected by the auth gate (commands never leave `delivered`)
findings.evidence: `src/app.ts:222` `const deviceFacingPaths = ['/heartbeat', '/telemetry', '/apps', '/commands/pending', '/events'];` then `src/app.ts:259` `authMiddleware(req, res, next);` which requires `Bearer <JWT>` (`src/middleware/auth.ts:55-60`). `PATCH /api/devices/:id/commands/:cmdId` (`app.ts:1239`) matches none of the device paths, so it goes to the admin JWT check. Android `CommandApiClient.kt:132` does `httpClient.patch("$baseUrl/api/devices/$deviceId/commands/$commandId")` and `createDefaultClient()` (`CommandApiClient.kt:34-41`) installs only ContentNegotiation: no Authorization or X-Session-Token header at all.
findings.scenario: admin queues REBOOT or INSTALL_APK. Device polls (`GET .../commands/pending` works only because the "no token -> next()" backward-compat branch at `app.ts:236` lets it through), executes it, then `markExecuting`/`markCompleted` get 401 and are retried 3 times then dropped (`CommandApiClient.kt:128-165`). Every command stays `delivered` forever, `command-completed`/`command-failed` events (`app.ts:1263-1290`) are never generated, and the UI can never tell success from failure. If the owner later fixes the "no token" hole (security), polling and ack would both break for the same reason, since the Android client sends no credential.
findings.fix: add the ack route to the device-facing set (`req.method === 'PATCH' && /\/commands\/[^/]+$/.test(path)`) and make the Android client send `X-Session-Token`. Also verify that the ack's `cmdId` belongs to `:id` (see SR-12). I could not run the tests, but `test/commands.test.ts:276-289` PATCHes with no auth and expects 200, so the tests contradict the current gate (see SR-14).

findings.title: Heartbeat silently consumes (and drops) queued commands
findings.evidence:
`src/app.ts:609-616`:
  `const appCount = appInventoryStore.getDeviceAppCount(id, true); if (appCount === 0) { const pendingCmds = commandStore.getPendingCommands(id); ...hasPendingSync...`. `getPendingCommands` (`commandStore.ts:133-163`) is a destructive read: it `UPDATE ... SET status='delivered'` on every pending row.
findings.scenario: freshly enrolled device (0 apps recorded) or a device whose app sync failed; admin queues INSTALL_APK/REBOOT; device sends `POST /heartbeat` before its next poll. The heartbeat handler flips all pending commands to `delivered` and throws the list away. The device's next poll returns nothing. The commands are lost and appear "delivered". Also, if SYNC_APPS was the one pending, `hasPendingSync` is computed from commands already marked delivered, so it re-queues SYNC_APPS on every heartbeat until apps arrive.
findings.fix: use the non-mutating `getPendingCount`/a new `hasPending(deviceId, 'SYNC_APPS')` (`SELECT 1 ... WHERE type='SYNC_APPS' AND status IN ('pending','delivered','executing')`).

findings.title: At-most-once delivery with no lease/redelivery: crash or network loss after poll loses the command; `executing` can stick forever
findings.evidence: `commandStore.ts:152-156` marks `delivered` in the same call that returns the rows; nothing ever moves `delivered`/`executing` back to `pending` (no timer anywhere: grep for `setInterval` finds only `relay.ts`). `acknowledgeCommand` only accepts forward transitions (`:195-207`).
findings.scenario: response to `GET /commands/pending` is lost (flaky mobile data, app killed, device reboot) -> server thinks delivered, device never saw it -> command never runs, never fails, no alert. Scenario B: device acks `executing` for REBOOT or a self-update INSTALL_APK (`CommandPollingService.kt:445-450` notes the process is killed) and the process dies before `completed` -> stays `executing` forever. The owner's three key operations (reboot, install, auto-start app) are exactly the ones that kill the app/device mid-flight.
findings.fix: add a lease: `delivered_at`/`lease_until`; poll returns rows `WHERE status='pending' OR (status IN ('delivered','executing') AND delivered_at < now-LEASE)`; cap attempts (`attempts` column, fail after N). Make the device-side idempotent by command id (INSTALL_APK of the same version is already idempotent, REBOOT/WIPE/LOCK are not, so for those prefer fail-after-timeout over redelivery). Wrap select+update in `db.transaction`.

findings.title: No command expiry: a device offline for days executes every stale command in order on return, including REBOOT/WIPE/LOCK
findings.evidence: `queueCommand` (`commandStore.ts:102-127`) has no `expires_at`/TTL; `getPendingCommands` has no age filter; schema has no such column (`schema.ts:316-330`).
findings.scenario: kiosk device is powered off for a week. Admin meanwhile queued REBOOT (retried 3 times by an impatient operator), LOCK, SCREEN_OFF, WIPE. On boot the device runs all of them back to back. A "reboot now" becomes a reboot loop of N reboots, as each REBOOT kills the app mid-list (and see SR-03: the rest are then lost or stuck `executing`). A WIPE queued "just in case" still executes days later.
findings.fix: `expires_at` per command type (e.g. 10 min for REBOOT/LOCK/SCREEN_*/START_REMOTE/TAKE_SCREENSHOT; days for INSTALL_APK/SYNC_POLICY); in `getPendingCommands` mark expired ones `failed` with error `expired`; surface in UI. Dedupe queued REBOOT/SYNC_APPS/SYNC_POLICY per device (see SR-08).

findings.title: Relay: reconnecting agent is torn down by the old socket's late `close` event
findings.evidence: `src/services/agentConnectionStore.ts:36-45` `addAgent` closes the existing socket (`existing.ws.close(1000, 'replaced by new connection')`) and stores the new connection under the same `deviceId`. The old socket's handler `relay.ts:210-217`: `ws.on('close', () => { ... agentConnectionStore.removeAgent(deviceId); deviceStore.updateDeviceStatus(deviceId, 'offline'); })` removes by `deviceId`, not by connection identity. Same for the `error` handler (`:219-225`) and for the `cleanupStale` path.
findings.scenario: agent's network flaps (very common for remote machines); server has not noticed the dead TCP yet (up to 90 s, SR-06); agent reconnects and authenticates; `addAgent` closes the old ws; when that `close` fires (immediately for a clean close, or later for the half-open one), it deletes the NEW connection from the map and marks the device offline. From then on `handleAgentMessage` does `const conn = getAgent(deviceId); if (!conn) return;` (`relay.ts:341-342`) so heartbeats/frames/telemetry from the live socket are ignored, viewers get `4004 agent not connected`, and nothing recovers until the agent reconnects again. The remote-control feature is dead while the agent believes it is connected.
findings.fix: in the close/error handlers, only remove if `agentConnectionStore.getAgent(deviceId)?.ws === ws` (add `removeAgentIfSocket(deviceId, ws)`), and only mark offline in that case.

findings.title: Relay/signaling: no ping/pong, no backpressure, no per-device/global session limits
findings.evidence: Only agents get an app-level heartbeat (`relay.ts:323-334`). Viewers (`relay.ts:495-589`), `/ws` peers and `/admin` sockets (`signaling.ts:197-259`) have no ping/pong or `isAlive` sweep. `sendBinary` (`relay.ts:645-649`) calls `ws.send(data)` with no `bufferedAmount` check or callback. `allocateChannel` (`agentConnectionStore.ts:121`) `conn.nextChannelId++` has no cap: channel id is encoded as `writeUInt16LE` (`relay.ts:64`) and wraps/throws after 65535 sessions, and nothing limits concurrent viewers per device.
findings.scenario: operator closes laptop lid / Wi-Fi drops while viewing: TCP stays half-open, the viewer ws stays in `activeSessions` and agent keeps encoding and sending 15 fps JPEG frames (`quality 70, fps 15`, `relay.ts:602`) into a socket that never drains; `ws` buffers them in memory without bound (frames per second x tens of KB) until the OS gives up (minutes to hours). Same for a slow browser tab. Scenario 2: the `/admin` and `/ws` half-open sockets accumulate in `adminConnections`/`rooms` and `broadcastEventToAdmins` keeps sending to them (`signaling.ts:62-76`). Scenario 3: `ws` default `maxPayload` is 100 MiB for all three servers (`new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`), larger than the protocol ever needs (u16 length, max 64 KiB).
findings.fix: server-side `ws.ping()` every 30 s with `isAlive` + `terminate()` for all three WSS; in `sendBinary` drop DESKTOP_FRAME frames when `ws.bufferedAmount > 1 MiB` (and close if it stays high); set `maxPayload: 70*1024`; cap viewers per device (e.g. 3) and recycle channel ids; send `DESKTOP_CLOSE` when the last viewer leaves (already done) and close agent sessions on viewer `error` (currently only `removeSession`, `relay.ts:586-588`; `close` normally follows, so low impact).

findings.title: Signaling: stale-peer replacement sends a spurious `peer-left` after the new peer has joined; double-join leaks room slots
findings.evidence: `signaling.ts:289-301` evicts the old peer (`delete room[role]; existingPeer.ws.close(...)`) and, before that, sends `peer-left` to the other side. Then the old ws's `close` fires `handleDisconnect(currentPeer)` (`:248-252`, `:355-375`); even though `room[peer.role] === peer` is false (so it does not delete the slot), the code still runs `send(otherPeer.ws, { type: 'peer-left' })` unconditionally (`:364-369`).
findings.scenario: the Android device (or controller) reconnects while the old socket is still registered (very common with mobile networks, the code comment says "so reconnects always succeed"). Sequence seen by the controller: `peer-left` (eviction), `peer-joined` (new device), then `peer-left` again when the old socket finally closes, so the controller tears down a just-negotiated WebRTC session. Also: a socket that sends `join` twice (different `deviceId`) overwrites `currentPeer` (`:303-305`) and leaves its first room slot occupied by a ws that is open but unreachable by close handling; the room is never cleaned until that ws closes, then `handleDisconnect` only handles the latest peer, so the first room keeps a dead `Peer` (readyState CLOSED) and later joiners get `peer-joined` to nothing (`send` silently skips non-OPEN).
findings.fix: in `handleDisconnect`, `if (room[peer.role] !== peer) return;` before notifying. Reject (or clean up) a second `join` from the same socket.

findings.title: Events table flood (battery alert every telemetry report) and no retention anywhere: unbounded DB growth
findings.evidence: `app.ts:1335-1349`: every `POST /telemetry` with `batteryLevel < 20` calls `eventStore.recordEvent({ eventType: 'battery-low' ...})`, with no dedupe, and `nextReportIn: 60000`. Purge helpers exist (`schema.ts:637-700`: `purgeTelemetryHistory`, `purgeOldEvents`, `purgeOldAuditLogs`, `purgeOldFileTransfers`, `purgeExpiredDeviceSessions`, `purgeOldSessions`) but grep over `src/` and `test/` shows no caller. Nothing at all prunes `device_commands` either.
findings.scenario: a kiosk device sits at 15% on a flaky charger: 1,440 `battery-low` events per day per device, 20 devices -> ~10 M rows/year, each also pushed over the admin WebSocket (`signaling.ts:56`). `device_events`, `audit_logs`, `device_commands`, `sessions` (expired rows) only grow. `/api/events` (SR-10) gets slower and SQLite file/WAL grows with no ceiling.
findings.fix: emit battery events only on threshold crossing (compare to previous `device_telemetry.battery_level`, or last event of that type within N hours); run a daily `setInterval(...).unref()` job in `index.ts` calling the existing purge functions plus `device_commands` older than 30-90 days in terminal state; `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` occasionally.

findings.title: Telemetry history is never written, so the history API/chart is always empty
findings.evidence: `telemetryStore.recordHistory` / `recordAllHistory` (`telemetryStore.ts:263-300`, doc comment "call periodically") have zero callers (grep `recordAllHistory|recordHistory` over `src/` and `test/`). `GET /api/devices/:id/telemetry/history` (`app.ts:1390`) reads only `telemetry_history`, which stays empty. The web UI hook `web-ui/src/hooks/useTelemetry.ts:91` calls it.
findings.scenario: owner opens a device's battery/storage trend: always "no data". The analytics requirement is only half met (latest snapshot only).
findings.fix: in the telemetry POST handler insert a history row when the last one is older than ~5 min (cheap, one INSERT), or schedule `recordAllHistory(10*60*1000)` every 5 min; add retention (SR-08). Also `updateTelemetry` uses `COALESCE(excluded.x, x)` (`:163-180`) so a field can never be cleared: SSID/IP/location stay at the last non-null value after the device goes to cellular or turns location off (stale data shown as current). Store `null` explicitly when the field key is present in the body.

findings.title: Missing indexes for the hot "recent first" queries
findings.evidence: Dashboard queries `SELECT * FROM device_events WHERE 1=1 ... ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?` (`eventStore.ts:231-260`, no device filter) and `SELECT * FROM device_commands ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?` (`commandStore.ts:254-258`); indexes present: `device_events(device_id, created_at)`, `(event_type, created_at)`, partial `(acknowledged, severity) WHERE acknowledged=0`; `device_commands(device_id)` and partial pending only (`schema.ts:333-338`). `getCommandHistory` (`commandStore.ts:222-245`) filters `device_id` (+status) and sorts `created_at DESC` using only `idx_device_commands_device`, so it sorts all of the device's commands each call. Also `ORDER BY created_at ASC` in `getPendingCommands` ties on equal ms (batch queue within one ms) and has no tie-break.
findings.scenario: with SR-08 volume, every dashboard events refresh scans/sorts millions of rows (events filtered by `severity`/`acknowledged` fall back to the same sort); command history for a chatty device slows linearly.
findings.fix: `CREATE INDEX idx_device_events_created ON device_events(created_at DESC)`; `CREATE INDEX idx_device_commands_dev_created ON device_commands(device_id, created_at DESC)` and `(created_at DESC)`; use `ORDER BY created_at, rowid` for pending. Cap `limit` server-side (`Math.min(limit, 500)`, handle NaN from `parseInt`; `app.ts:1229`, `2437`, `2449`, ... accept any value).

findings.title: APK upload buffers up to 500 MB in RAM per request; no cleanup on DB failure; orphaned files
findings.evidence: `app.ts:36-38` `multer({ storage: multer.memoryStorage(), limits: { fileSize: 500 * 1024 * 1024 } })`; `storageProvider.ts` `save(filename, data: Buffer)` -> `fs.promises.writeFile(filePath, data)`; agent binary (`app.ts:771`, 200 MB) and installer (`:1003`, 200 MB) uploads also use memoryStorage. In `app.ts:1542-1610` the file is written first, then `createAppPackage`/`updateAppPackage`; if the DB step throws, the file is left on disk.
findings.scenario: one 400 MB APK upload costs 400 MB heap-external buffer (plus multer copy); two concurrent uploads (or a retry after a timeout) can OOM a small VPS container and take the MDM down (and with it every device's polling). Real Android APKs are rarely >150 MB, but the limit invites it.
findings.fix: `multer.diskStorage` into `uploads/tmp`, then `fs.rename` into place (streaming), lower the limit to what you need (e.g. 200 MB), delete the written file in the `catch`. `StorageProvider.save` should accept a stream/path.

findings.title: Command bookkeeping is not scoped to the device in the URL
findings.evidence: `app.ts:1239-1297` takes `:id` only for the event's `deviceId`; `acknowledgeCommand(cmdId, ...)`/`cancelCommand(cmdId)` ignore it (`commandStore.ts:184-210`, `:281-291`). `GET /devices/:id/commands/pending` etc. fine.
findings.scenario: a stale/buggy device (or cloned device id) acking `cmd-X` that belongs to another device marks it completed and emits a `command-completed` event under the wrong device.
findings.fix: `WHERE id = ? AND device_id = ?`.

findings.title: Process-level error handling and graceful shutdown absent
findings.evidence: `src/index.ts` (34 lines) has no `process.on('SIGTERM'|'SIGINT')`, no `unhandledRejection`/`uncaughtException`, never calls `shutdownRelay()` (`relay.ts:149`, defined but unused) or `closeDatabase()` (`db/connection.ts:39`). No Express async-error wrapper: handlers are sync, so thrown errors reach the error middleware (`app.ts:2809`), but code in `ws.on('message')` handlers is not wrapped: `handleAgentMessage`/`relayToViewer` (`relay.ts:174-208`, `549-574`) throw on e.g. `writeUInt16LE` out of range, and an exception inside an EventEmitter callback is an uncaught exception that kills the whole process (all devices drop). `handleAgentAuth(...).then(...)` (`relay.ts:193`) has no `.catch`.
findings.scenario: `docker stop`/deploy sends SIGTERM -> process dies without closing WS clients or checkpointing WAL (clients see abrupt reset; fine functionally but noisy); a malformed frame from one agent/viewer path that throws takes down the server.
findings.fix: wrap message handlers in try/catch and `ws.close(1011)`; add SIGTERM/SIGINT handler: stop accepting, `shutdownRelay()`, close WSS, `server.close()`, `closeDatabase()`, with a 10 s force-exit; log `unhandledRejection`.

findings.title: Test suite does not cover the critical paths and appears stale against current code
findings.evidence: `test/` has 7 files (1,595 lines). No test for relay.ts (only `signaling.test.ts`, 4 incidental mentions), agentConnectionStore, telemetry/events/audit stores, app upload, appSyncService, command expiry/redelivery. `commands.test.ts:28-40` POSTs `/api/devices/test-device/commands` and PATCHes acks with no Authorization header and reads `cmd.body.id`, but the handler path is behind the `/api` gate (`app.ts:194-259`, JWT required for non-device paths) and returns `{ command }` (`app.ts:1201`-ish). `signaling.test.ts:109-137` "rejects duplicate role in same room" expects `{type:'error', message:'Role device already taken in this room'}`, but `signaling.ts:287-301` now evicts the old peer instead and never sends that error. (Based on reading; jest not run.)
findings.scenario: SR-01, SR-02, SR-05, SR-07 shipped because nothing exercises the real device flow end to end (device token -> poll -> ack, heartbeat with empty inventory, agent reconnect).
findings.fix: first make the suite green (adapt auth in `test/setup.ts`, fix the two stale expectations), then add: heartbeat-does-not-consume-pending (SR-02), ack with device token (SR-01), redelivery/expiry (SR-03/04), relay reconnect-with-late-close (SR-05), peer-left ordering (SR-07).

findings.title: `updateDeviceStatus('offline')` wipes `last_seen_at`
findings.evidence: `deviceStore.ts:236-239` `UPDATE devices SET status = ?, last_seen_at = ? ...run(status, status === 'online' ? Date.now() : null, id)`.
findings.scenario: when a relay agent disconnects, `last_seen_at` becomes NULL; the UI shows "never seen" for a machine that was online a minute ago, and `rowToDevice` (`:430-444`) computes status only from `last_seen_at`.
findings.fix: only set `last_seen_at` for online; leave it untouched on offline. Related: `device-offline` events exist as a type (`eventStore.ts:9`) but nothing ever emits them (only `device-online` at `app.ts:596`), because Android status is derived on read and no sweeper exists. Add a periodic sweeper (e.g. every 60 s: devices with `last_seen_at < now-2min` and no recent offline event -> `device-offline` event). This directly serves the owner's "know when a kiosk is down" need.

findings.title: Command-schema migration is unsafe and non-transactional
findings.evidence: `schema.ts:276-330`: when `COMMAND_TYPES` has a type that the stored CREATE SQL lacks, the code renames to `device_commands_old`, creates the new table, copies rows `WHERE type IN (...)` (silently dropping rows with unknown types), then drops the old table, all via separate `db.exec` calls with no `db.transaction`. It is also re-run on every `initializeSchema` call (each store calls it, `commandStore.ts:67-72`).
findings.scenario: crash between RENAME and CREATE/INSERT leaves the server without a `device_commands` table (next start sees none and creates empty, history lost) with data stranded in `device_commands_old`. Adding a new command type to the list triggers this on the next start.
findings.fix: wrap in `db.transaction`, or drop the CHECK constraint and validate types in code (the app already validates with `COMMAND_TYPES.includes`), and use `PRAGMA user_version` migrations.

findings.title: `app.ts` monolith: concrete maintainability problems
findings.evidence: 2,825 lines, ~110 routes registered directly with `app.<verb>`; auth gate is a hand-written substring matcher (`app.ts:194-259`, `path.includes('/apps')`, `'/events'`, `'/commands/pending'`) that already caused SR-01 and is easy to get wrong (e.g. `path.includes('/policy')` and `/app-updates` make any GET path containing those strings device-public). Copy-pasted "install to devices + enrich with policy" blocks in `app.ts:1090-1113`, `1696-1716`, `1757-1776`, and `appSyncService.ts:22-31`, with slightly different payloads (the `appSyncService` version omits `appName`/`versionName`, others include them), so behavior depends on which route queued the command. `parseInt(limit as string, 10)` repeated ~15 times without NaN/cap handling.
findings.fix: split into `routes/{devices,commands,apps,policies,events,files,audit}.ts` mounted on `express.Router()`; register device-facing routes on a separate `/api/device` router with its own middleware (`requireDeviceToken`) instead of a substring list; one `buildInstallPayload(device, pkg)` helper; a shared `parsePagination(req)`.

findings.title: Duplicate command pile-up from policy sync
findings.evidence: `app.ts:2259-2280` queues `INSTALL_APK` (via `syncPolicyRequiredApps`, `appSyncService.ts:48-62`) plus `SYNC_POLICY` to every device with the policy on every policy edit that touches `requiredApps/silentMode/kioskMode`, and `app.ts:2400-2410` again on policy assignment; no check whether the app is already installed at that versionCode or an identical command is already pending.
findings.scenario: admin edits a policy 5 times while a store kiosk is offline -> 5 INSTALL_APK (same APK, each a download of up to hundreds of MB) and 5 SYNC_POLICY wait; on reconnect all run (with SR-04 no expiry). Wastes mobile data and time-to-ready.
findings.fix: before queueing, skip if an identical `(device_id, type, payload)` is `pending`/`delivered`; for INSTALL_APK compare with `device_apps.version_code`; for SYNC_POLICY, supersede older pending ones (delete or mark `failed: superseded`).

findings.title: Enrollment-token endpoints are unauthenticated (the UI never sends a token)
findings.evidence: web-ui/src/components/EnrollmentModal.tsx:84 and :114 and :184 use raw `fetch(\`${API_BASE_URL}/api/enroll/tokens\`...)` with no Authorization header. server/src/app.ts:195-202 whitelists the `'/enroll/'` prefix as public. server/src/app.ts:629 `app.post('/api/enroll/tokens', (req, res) =>`, :643 `app.get('/api/enroll/tokens'` and :654 `app.delete(...)` have no `authMiddleware`.
findings.scenario: any host that can reach the server runs `curl -X POST /api/enroll/tokens -d '{"maxUses":100}'`. It gets a valid token, enrolls a rogue device or agent, and lists or revokes everyone's tokens. The UI works only because the endpoints are open. Enrollment is therefore not an admin-gated action.
findings.fix: add `authMiddleware` to the three routes, or split the public `/enroll/device` route out of the prefix whitelist. In the UI use `apiFetch` in the three places. Keep only `POST /api/enroll/device` public.

findings.title: Signaling `/ws` and admin `/admin` WebSockets carry no authentication from the UI, and the server does not check one
findings.evidence: web-ui/src/hooks/useWebRTC.ts:217 `new WebSocket(signalingUrl)` then :312 `{type:'join', deviceId, role:'controller'}` with no token. useAdminWebSocket.ts:44 `new WebSocket(\`${WS_BASE}/admin\`)` also has no token. server/src/signaling.ts:178-190 upgrades `/ws` and `/admin` with no check. signaling.ts:272-314 lets any peer join any `deviceId` as controller and "evict the stale peer" (lines 287-299).
findings.scenario: an unauthenticated client opens `/ws`, joins `{deviceId: X, role:'controller'}`, evicts the real admin session, and gets a WebRTC data channel to the device. That channel carries TAP/KEY_PRESS/TYPE_TEXT/INSTALL_APP/WIPE_DEVICE (types in useWebRTC.ts:8-25). Whether the Android side gates these is for the Android reviewer. Separately, `/admin` streams all device events (`data` payloads included, signaling.ts:61-75) to any anonymous client.
findings.fix: require a JWT (query param or first message) on `/ws` controller join and on `/admin`, verified in the `upgrade` handler before `handleUpgrade`. The device role must authenticate with its session token. Do not let a later join evict an authenticated controller.

findings.title: Realtime admin events never reach the UI (event name mismatch), so Events and Dashboard are stale
findings.evidence: the server only emits `type: 'device-event'` (server/src/signaling.ts:65). The UI subscribes to `'event-created'`, `'device-online'` and `'device-offline'` (useAdminWebSocket.ts:7-14, :146, :152, :174). A grep of server/src finds none of these as WS message types. `device-online` appears only as an eventType value (eventStore.ts:8).
findings.scenario: EventsPage (pages/EventsPage.tsx:214) fetches once and relies on `useRealtimeEvents`, so a new critical alert never shows until the user reloads. The Dashboard "recent events" feed never updates. The only live signal is the 10 s device poll.
findings.fix: subscribe to `'device-event'` and switch on `msg.event.eventType`. Alternatively make the server emit the types the UI expects. Add a contract test.

findings.title: Admin WebSocket hook: zombie reconnect loop after unmount, plus a socket per hook call
findings.evidence: useAdminWebSocket.ts:52-56 `ws.onclose = () => {... reconnectTimeoutRef.current = setTimeout(connect, 5000)}`. The cleanup at :87-91 runs `clearTimeout(...)` and then `wsRef.current?.close()`. The close event fires after the clear, so `onclose` schedules a new timer and `connect` runs again. There is no `unmounted` flag. Every call of `useAdminWebSocket`, `useRealtimeEvents` or `useRealtimeDeviceStatus` also creates its own socket. Dashboard.tsx:193-194 calls two, so it opens two sockets.
findings.scenario: navigate Dashboard -> Devices -> Events -> ... Each unmounted hook instance keeps reconnecting every 5 s forever. Open `/admin` sockets pile up per tab, and each receives every broadcast. Also no backoff and no auth-failure handling.
findings.fix: an `unmountedRef` checked in `onclose`, or null `ws.onclose` before `close()`. Better, a single module-level or context-provided socket with ref-counted subscribers, and exponential backoff with jitter.

findings.title: Android remote: tap/swipe coordinates are wrong when the canvas box is letterboxed
findings.evidence: RemoteScreen.tsx:296-305 `width:'100%', maxWidth:'400px', maxHeight:'80vh', aspectRatio, objectFit:'contain'`. getNormalizedCoordinates (:111-118) divides by `rect.width/rect.height`, the whole element box.
findings.scenario: when `maxHeight: 80vh` clamps the height (a laptop window under ~890 px tall with a 9:16 device), the width stays 400 px, so the box no longer has the video aspect ratio. `object-fit: contain` letterboxes the picture inside the box, but normalized (0..1) coordinates are still computed over the full box. Taps land offset horizontally, growing toward the edges, and the Back/Home regions are missed.
findings.fix: compute the displayed video rect from `videoDimensions` (contain math) and map `(clientX - letterboxLeft)/drawnWidth`. Or size the canvas by `min(containerW/ar, containerH)` so box and video always match. Reject taps in the bars.

findings.title: Android remote: a pointer released outside the canvas fires a spurious long press and gets lost
findings.evidence: RemoteScreen.tsx:121-199 has handlers for down/move/up only. There is no `setPointerCapture`, `onPointerLeave` or `onPointerCancel`, and the long-press timer (:132) is cleared only in `pointerMove` beyond the threshold (:150) or in `pointerUp` (:158).
findings.scenario: the user presses on the canvas, drags off it and releases. `pointerUp` never fires. The move handler stops once the pointer leaves (events are no longer delivered to the canvas), so the 500 ms timer is not cancelled and a LONG_PRESS is sent at the original point. `pointerStartRef` stays set, so the next click is treated as the end of a swipe from a stale origin.
findings.fix: `e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` on down, and handle `onPointerCancel` and `onLostPointerCapture` by clearing the timer and state. Add `touch-action: none` for touch screens.

findings.title: H.264 decoder: decode errors are only logged; the stream silently freezes while the UI shows "connected"
findings.evidence: FrameDecoder.ts:66-69 `error: (e) => console.error('Decode error:', e)`. After an async error the VideoDecoder goes to `closed`, and decodeFrame (:257) then returns silently with `if (!this.decoder || this.decoder.state === 'closed') return;`. Nothing re-creates the decoder or asks the device for a keyframe.
findings.scenario: one corrupt NAL, an SPS change or a hardware-decoder hiccup closes the decoder. The canvas freezes on the last frame, `connectionState` is still 'connected', and nothing is shown to the operator. Their taps still go through to the device and land on a screen they cannot see (dangerous with reboot, wipe or install dialogs).
findings.fix: in `error`, mark the decoder dead, call `initDecoder()` again, set `configured=false`, drop frames until the next IDR, and request a keyframe over the data channel (a `REQUEST_KEYFRAME` command, if the device supports it). Show a "video lost, reconnecting" overlay and surface it to the parent.

findings.title: H.264 decoder: no backlog or latency control, unbounded pre-keyframe queue, no resync after a dropped frame
findings.evidence: FrameDecoder.ts:134-153 decodes every frame on arrival. `decoder.decodeQueueSize` is never read. `renderFrame` (:292-303) draws each output synchronously (acceptable, but frames are never skipped). `pendingFrames.push(data)` at :249 has no cap or age limit and holds delta frames received before the first IDR. configure() (:123-127) flushes those deltas before the keyframe, so they error (swallowed by the try/catch at :287). A stale-chunk GC at :207-213 silently drops incomplete frames and the next delta frames decode against a missing reference.
findings.scenario: the browser tab throttles in the background or the network stalls. Frames queue in the decoder, and on resume the view plays seconds of backlog (latency does not shrink). If a device never sends an IDR after a reconnect, `pendingFrames` grows without bound (memory). A GC'd chunk produces smeared artefacts until the next periodic keyframe, with no resync.
findings.fix: if `decoder.decodeQueueSize > N` (e.g. 3), drop deltas until the next keyframe. Cap or discard `pendingFrames` (keep none, only wait for IDR). When a chunk set is GC'd, set `needKeyframe=true` and ignore deltas until an IDR. Draw with `requestAnimationFrame`, latest-frame-wins.

findings.title: WebRTC connect flow: `ws.onclose` closure is stale, failures are swallowed, and a fixed 6 s sleep replaces real signalling
findings.evidence: useWebRTC.ts:367-372 `ws.onclose = () => { if (connectionState === 'connecting') {...}}` captures the render-time state, so the branch is effectively dead and a signalling close is never reported. DeviceRemote.tsx:77-80 only `console.error`s a failed START_REMOTE and carries on. :87 `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 6000))`, then `setPhase('active')` regardless.
findings.scenario: the device is offline or START_REMOTE returns 4xx/5xx. The operator waits 6 s on "Sending connection request", then sees "Connecting..." forever or a generic "Connection failed", with no reason. If the device takes 7 s to start its session, the 'peer-joined' offer path may race.
findings.fix: surface `response.ok === false` (and an offline device) as an error and do not enter 'active'. Replace the sleep with waiting for the device `peer-joined` event, with a timeout. Use a ref for state in `onclose`. Add a connect timeout (e.g. 20 s) that moves to 'failed'.

findings.title: There is no WebRTC -> relay fallback for Android, and ICE relies on hard-coded public TURN credentials
findings.evidence: DeviceRemote.tsx:33-39 chooses by `osType`: android -> WebRTC only, others -> relay only. useWebRTC.ts:105-120 hard-codes Google STUN and a public Metered "Open Relay" TURN `username: 'e8dd65b92f3aef1c190c914f', credential: '4F2oRAyF/Br8Xijx'` shipped in the JS bundle.
findings.scenario: devices behind symmetric NAT or restrictive networks depend on the shared public TURN (rate-limited, shared by strangers, can disappear). When the connection fails there is no automatic alternative path, only "Connection failed". Anyone can read the credential. The traffic is DTLS-encrypted, but this is a third-party dependency for a core feature.
findings.fix: serve short-lived TURN credentials from your own coturn via an authenticated `/api/turn` endpoint (use-time HMAC credentials). Add a retry or an "ICE restart" and a documented fallback path.

findings.title: Relay desktop: tiles are decoded concurrently and can be drawn out of order; no input coalescing; no reconnect; stuck keys
findings.evidence: RelayRemoteScreen.tsx:333-361 `renderTile` is `async` and fires `await createImageBitmap(blob)` per tile with no ordering or concurrency limit. Draw order equals decode completion order. `bitmap.close()` is called (no leak) and errors are silently ignored (:358). handleMouseMove (:109-120) sends one WS message per `mousemove` with no `requestAnimationFrame` throttle, and `useRelayWebSocket.send` ignores `bufferedAmount` (:151-155). useRelayWebSocket.ts:128-133 `onclose` has no auto reconnect. There is no `onBlur` or `mouseleave` handler, so key-up and mouse-up are missed when focus is lost.
findings.scenario: two tiles of the same region arrive back to back, the older JPEG finishes later and overwrites the newer pixels, which leaves stale rectangles on screen until the region changes again. Moving a high-rate mouse floods the WS (up to ~1000 msg/s) and queues behind the frame stream, causing laggy input. Alt-tab with Ctrl held leaves Ctrl stuck on the remote. Dropping the WS shows "Disconnected" with no auto-retry. Also, `readBufferRef` re-concatenates the whole buffer per message (useRelayWebSocket.ts:99-105), which is O(n^2) for fragmented frames.
findings.fix: decode tiles in a serial promise chain or tag each with a sequence number and drop stale ones. Coalesce mouse moves to one per animation frame (latest wins) and skip when `ws.bufferedAmount` is high. Send key-up for held keys on `blur`, and mouse-up on a window-level `mouseup`. Add exponential-backoff reconnect.

findings.title: Relay session token travels in the WebSocket URL
findings.evidence: useRelayWebSocket.ts:50 `.../relay?deviceId=...&session=...&token=${encodeURIComponent(token)}`, and an identical copy in DeviceRemote.tsx:24. The token is the full 24 h admin JWT (middleware/auth.ts:111 `expiresIn: '24h'`).
findings.scenario: a reverse proxy, CDN or server access log records the URL, leaking a full admin JWT valid for 24 h to anyone with log access. A relay session token would be the same credential as the admin API.
findings.fix: obtain a single-use, short-lived (e.g. 30 s) relay ticket from `POST /api/relay/ticket` and put that in the URL. Or send the JWT in the first WS message. Also drop the unused duplicate `getRelayUrl` export from DeviceRemote.tsx.

findings.title: Reboot (and other destructive quick actions) need no confirmation, and command failures are only logged
findings.evidence: DeviceCommands.tsx:73-80 `onClick={() => handleCommand(() => CommandHelpers.reboot(sendCommand), 'reboot')}` has no `confirm`. handleCommand (:19-28) is `catch (err) { console.error(...) }` with no UI error. useCommands.ts:125 throws on `!res.ok`, which gets swallowed there. The same pattern is in AppsPage.tsx:218-232 (`console.error('Failed to deploy:', err)`) and :153 `handleStatusChange`. EventsPage.tsx:156-164 swallows ack errors.
findings.scenario: a mis-click reboots a kiosk device in front of customers. A command rejected by the server (validation, 401, device not found) only appears in the devtools console. The operator sees the button spinner stop and assumes it worked. The history list refreshes only if the POST succeeded.
findings.fix: a `ConfirmDialog` for reboot, lock, wipe, uninstall and deploy-to-all. In the catch, show the error in a toast or inline banner. After the POST succeeds, show the created command status (pending/delivered/failed) inline.

findings.title: Install-then-reboot race and unchecked results in the app install flow
findings.evidence: InstallApkModal.tsx:20 `useState(true)` for `rebootAfterInstall` (default on). :85-100: `await onInstall(...)` (queues INSTALL_APK) then immediately `Promise.all(deviceIds.map(... apiFetch(... type:'REBOOT')))` with no `res.ok` check, then `onClose()`. :162-170 offline devices are selectable.
findings.scenario: both commands are queued (device polls CommandPollingService). A device that fetches both in one poll, or downloads the APK slowly, may reboot before the install finishes (the install is lost or half-applied), and the user sees a success close. A failed REBOOT POST (401, rate limit) passes unnoticed. Offline devices get queued commands with no indication that they won't run until the device is back (and the stale install may run days later).
findings.fix: make reboot conditional on the install command reaching `completed` (server-side chained command, or a poll of the install command status). Leave the default off or require explicit opt-in. Check each response and report per-device results (success/failed/offline) in the modal before closing.

findings.title: Kiosk / auto-start-on-boot has no UI path beyond a policy checkbox, and no way to see whether it was applied
findings.evidence: kiosk exists only as policy fields (PoliciesPage.tsx:179-200, :355-359; PolicyDetailPage.tsx:349-351). A grep of pages/components/hooks for boot, autostart or LAUNCH_APP finds only `CommandHelpers.launchApp` (useCommands.ts:154), which has no caller in any component. DeviceCommands has no apply-status for policy, only "Reapply Policy" (:113-120).
findings.scenario: the owner wants "app X starts on boot". They can set the kiosk package in a policy, but the device page never shows whether the policy was applied or whether the launcher or boot receiver is active. There is also no button to launch the app now. Per-device compliance appears only on the Dashboard count.
findings.fix: show per-device policy-applied state and the last SYNC_POLICY result in DeviceOverview, add "Launch app" to the app list, and show the effective boot app.

findings.title: Polling: duplicate and unbounded fetches, no backoff, and the full device list is fetched every 10 s (plus per-event refetch)
findings.evidence: useDevices.ts:68 `setInterval(() => fetchDevices(false), 10000)` and :132 `fetchDevice` every 5 s, neither with visibility or backoff handling. Dashboard.tsx:160-166 calls `refresh()` on every device-online/offline message (a full `GET /api/devices` per message). useTelemetry.ts:62 and :138 poll every 30 s (`/api/telemetry` returns every device). useCommands.ts:105-114 re-arms an interval per commands change. EnrollmentModal.tsx:112 polls `/api/enroll/tokens` (all tokens) every 2 s with `console.log` noise. Dashboard and DeviceDetail can mount `useDevices` plus the single-device hook together. On error the interval simply keeps retrying at the same rate.
findings.scenario: 500 devices, several admin tabs: each tab pulls the full device array every 10 s and the whole fleet's telemetry every 30 s, even when hidden. Once WU-03 is fixed, a fleet-wide reconnect (server restart) triggers N refetches in a burst.
findings.fix: pause intervals when `document.hidden`, add exponential backoff on failure, debounce event-triggered refreshes (e.g. 2 s), poll one device token by id instead of listing all, and prefer server push (the admin WS) with a slow poll as a safety net.

findings.title: Lists are fetched whole with no pagination or virtualization (devices, events, audit, apps, telemetry)
findings.evidence: DevicesPage.tsx:232 `devices.map(...)` renders every device card. DataTable.tsx renders all rows (DeviceApps.tsx:90). useEvents.ts:22-45 never sends `limit` or `offset`; the server default is 100 (server/src/app.ts:2437, :2449). useAudit supports `limit`/`offset` (useAudit.ts:7-16) but AuditPage.tsx:168 `useAudit(filters)` passes none, and its `total` is not used for paging (grep shows no `total` in AuditPage). useAllTelemetry (:117-143) returns all devices every 30 s.
findings.scenario: events and audit show only the newest 100 with no indicator that older ones exist; the operator cannot reach older audit records (the CSV export is the only way). Large fleets render every device card and each poll re-renders them all.
findings.fix: add pager or infinite scroll with `limit`/`offset` and show `total`. Use server-side search and filter for devices and virtualize large tables/cards (e.g. react-window). Add a "showing 100 of N" banner as a stopgap.

findings.title: Admin JWT lives in localStorage, and logout is client-only
findings.evidence: useAuth.tsx:25-26 and utils/api.ts:14 read `localStorage.getItem('auth_token')`. :35-36 write it. logout (:44-50) just removes the keys. The JWT is signed with 24 h expiry and there is no server-side revoke endpoint (grep for `logout` in server/src/app.ts and middleware/auth.ts finds none).
findings.scenario: any future XSS (a dependency or an injected third-party script is blocked by CSP today) exfiltrates a 24 h admin token that also authorizes remote control and WIPE. A stolen token cannot be invalidated by logging out.
findings.fix: put the session in an httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie (with CSRF protection) or at minimum shorten the token life plus a refresh flow, and add a server-side `jti` denylist so logout revokes. Tighten CSP: `connect-src` currently allows any `ws:`/`wss:` host (index.html:7), pin it to `'self'`.

findings.title: Chart/analytics data: raw telemetry history is fetched unbounded and there are no charts built in the UI
findings.evidence: useTelemetryHistory (hooks/useTelemetry.ts:76-108) returns `data.history` with no downsample or limit parameter and sends `from`/`to` only if provided. No component imports it (grep for `useTelemetryHistory|Chart` in components/pages finds only the hook), so the Dashboard shows counters only.
findings.scenario: the owner wants "device analytics". The data path exists but UI-side there are no trend views, and when one is added the unbounded fetch will return every sample for the range. This is a gap against the stated need rather than a bug today.
findings.fix: add `limit`/bucketed aggregation (`?bucket=5m`) to the endpoint and a battery/storage trend chart on DeviceOverview.

findings.title: Misc. smaller defects
findings.evidence:
• FileBrowser.tsx:95 uploads with raw `fetch('/api/files/upload')`, no Authorization header, so the upload fails with 401 (or is unprotected if the route is public). Use `apiFetch`.
• RemoteScreen.tsx:122, :180, :190 and useWebRTC.ts:145 log every pointer event and every command to the console (including TYPE_TEXT command payload sizes). Typed text is not logged, but ICE candidate strings (host IPs) are logged at useWebRTC.ts:273.
• useWebRTC.ts:181 `setTimeout` for the command timeout is never cleared, and pending promises are not rejected on unmount or disconnect (leaks 30 s timers, harmless but noisy).
• main.tsx:8-10 the comment says StrictMode is disabled because effects run twice break WebSocket connections: that is a sign the connect effects lack proper cleanup (see WU-04, WU-09).
• RemoteScreen.tsx has no wheel/scroll or pinch handler although SCROLL and PINCH commands exist (useWebRTC.ts:15-16), so scrolling needs swipe gestures only.
• useRelayWebSocket.ts:113 compares `channelId` captured in the closure (always null at connect time), so `setChannelId` runs for each message. Harmless render churn.
• vite.config.ts:25 `server.host: true` exposes the dev server to the LAN, and the proxy sets `secure:false`. Dev-only.

findings.title: No device-side authorization; any peer in the signaling room can drive input, WIPE, reboot and lock
findings.evidence:
- `SessionController.kt:176-179`: `commandChannel.commands.collect { envelope -> processCommand(...) }` runs everything with no check of who sent it.
  - `SessionController.kt:399-400`: `is RemoteCommand.WipeDevice -> handleMdmCommand { it.handleWipeDevice(command) }`, plus `RebootDevice`, `LockDevice`.
  - `SignalingClient.kt:~100`: the device joins with `SignalingMessage.Join(deviceId, role="device")`, with no token (`KtorWebSocketProvider.connect(serverUrl, emptyMap())`, `RemoteSession.kt` `webSocketProvider.connect`).
  - `server/src/signaling.ts:~213`: `case 'join'` stores `{deviceId, role}` with no authentication and evicts an existing peer ("Replacing stale ${role}"). The `/ws` upgrade (`signaling.ts:~163`) has no auth either. The JWT gate in `app.ts:194` covers only `/api`.
  - The `START_REMOTE` URL carries no ticket (`app.ts:327-331`: `${wsUrl}/ws`).
findings.scenario: anyone who can reach the server and knows or guesses a `deviceId` (ids look like `device-abc123`, per the comment at `app.ts:220`) opens `/ws`, joins that room as `controller` and evicts the legitimate browser. The device's WebSocket stays in the room indefinitely (see AR-03). The attacker sends an SDP offer. The device answers, and the attacker can view the screen and send TAP, KEY_PRESS, TYPE_TEXT (root shell, AR-02), `REBOOT_DEVICE`, `LOCK_DEVICE` and `WIPE_DEVICE`. Joining as `device` instead hijacks the viewer's session. Even with a fixed server, a rogue browser user gets destructive MDM commands over a channel that bypasses the per-device command queue and its audit trail.
findings.fix:
- Server: require a JWT on the WS upgrade, bind it to deviceId and role, and issue the device a per-session ticket (`START_REMOTE` payload `ticket`; the device sends it in `join`).
  - Device (defence in depth): on the data channel, require a first message `AUTH{nonce-signed-by-server}` before any command is accepted. The device can verify an HMAC with its existing enrolment session token.
  - Remove `WipeDevice`, `RebootDevice`, `InstallApp` and `UninstallApp` from the data-channel `RemoteCommand` union. The authenticated polling queue already handles them (`executeReboot`, `executeWipe`). Install and Uninstall are stubs anyway (`MdmHandler.kt` TODO).

findings.title: TYPE_TEXT is a root shell injection (newline not escaped)
findings.evidence: `AdbShellInjector.kt:80-81` `runShellCommand("input text $escaped")`, then `:132` `arrayOf("su","0","sh","-c", command)`. `escapeForShell` (`:169-195`) handles space, quotes, `\ ` `` ` `` `$ & | ; < > ( ) [ ] { }` but not `\n`, `\r`, `*`, `?`, `#`, `~`, `!`, `%`, `-`, or tab.
findings.scenario:
- Deliberate: `{"command":{"type":"TYPE_TEXT","text":"x\nsettings put global adb_enabled 1\nsu ..."}}`. `sh -c` treats the newline as a command separator, so the second line runs as root (uid 0).
  - Accidental, with no attacker: an operator pastes multi-line text into the remote keyboard (for example a Wi-Fi password followed by Enter). The second line executes as root, and `*`/`?` are glob-expanded.
findings.fix:
do not build a shell string.
  - Use `ProcessBuilder("su","0","input","text", text)` with the text as its own argv element. The `su -c` variant is different: its command is re-parsed, so quote the text in single quotes (`'` -> `'\''`) or pass it through stdin.
  - Replace spaces with `%s` only, and reject `\n`/control characters (send Enter as `keyevent 66`).
  - Cap text length.
  - Non-ASCII is not supported by `input text`; use the accessibility `setText` path for that.

findings.title: Capture and encoder keep running after the viewer leaves; the session never ends on the device
findings.evidence:
- `RemoteSessionService.kt:210-215`: capture stops only on `SessionState.Disconnected` or `Error`.
  - `SessionController.kt:306-308`: an unexpected drop goes to `Reconnecting`, not `Disconnected`.
  - `SessionController.kt:257-260`: `performConnect` ends with `session.connect(); session.startAsAnswerer()` and no timeout. It waits forever for an offer, and the state stays `Connecting`.
  - `reconnectAttempt` is reset only on `CONNECTED`, so waiting is never counted as a failure.
  - `SignalingClient` has `peerLeft` and `errors` flows that nothing collects (grep: no consumers in `app/src/main` or `core-transport/src/main`).
  - `screen-server/Server.kt:61-74`: the encoder runs as long as the socket stays open.
findings.scenario: an admin opens Remote, then closes the tab. The browser's `pc.close()` leads to ICE disconnected/failed on the device about 30 s later. The device enters `Reconnecting`/`Connecting`, rejoins the signaling room and waits indefinitely. `isScreenCaptureActive` stays true. The root-run screen-server keeps hardware-encoding 1080p at up to 60 fps and 8 Mbps (`SurfaceEncoder` defaults, no args passed by `startViaRoot`), and `ScreenServerClient` keeps copying frames into a flow with no subscriber. That drains CPU and battery 24/7 until the next START_REMOTE or reboot. On a kiosk player this causes heat, and a second STOP is never sent. The device's WebSocket also stays open in the room (feeds AR-01).
findings.fix:
- Collect `signalingClient.peerLeft`, and the data-channel `CLOSED` state, to call `stopScreenCapture()` and `disconnect()` after a short grace (about 10 s).
  - Add an overall idle timeout in the `Connecting`/`Reconnecting` state (for example 60 s without `CONNECTED` leads to teardown and `stopScreenCapture`).
  - Make the screen-server stop the encoder when no client is connected (it already does on broken pipe; the real fix is the app side).

findings.title: Video never restarts after a reconnect, and a transient ICE "disconnected" is treated as fatal
findings.evidence:
- `SessionController.kt:302-309`: `DISCONNECTED -> { stopVideoStream(); if (wasConnected && _state.value.isConnected) startReconnectSequence() }`, which tears the whole `PeerConnection` down and builds a new one.
  - `PeerConnectionWrapper.kt:~92-100`: ICE `DISCONNECTED` is mapped straight to connection state `DISCONNECTED`. libwebrtc raises this transiently for a few seconds on Wi-Fi roam or short loss, and it usually recovers without intervention.
  - `RemoteSessionService.kt:198`: the only place that starts video is `state is Connected && isAutoStartedSession && !isScreenCaptureActive`. `isAutoStartedSession` was set false on the first start (`:200`) and `isScreenCaptureActive` is still true, so the reconnected session gets no `startVideoStream` (the only call sites are `:408` and `:433`).
findings.scenario: a 3 s Wi-Fi blip tears down the session. Even if the reconnect succeeds, input may work but the screen stays black until the operator sends a new START_REMOTE. (It is also doubtful that the browser side can renegotiate: `useWebRTC.ts:281-290` creates a new offer on the same `RTCPeerConnection` after `peer-joined`, whose SCTP and ICE are already dead. So after any blip the user must reload and re-request the remote session anyway.)
findings.fix:
- Do not tear down on ICE `DISCONNECTED`. Wait about 8-10 s for recovery, and only treat `FAILED` or a persistent `DISCONNECTED` as fatal.
  - Put "start video on every `Connected`" into the state observer (call `startVideoStream(frameDataFlow)` on each `Connected` while `isScreenCaptureActive`), not behind a one-shot flag.
  - Have the browser hook rebuild the pc on `peer-joined`.

findings.title: Command and ICE pipes are `MutableSharedFlow(replay=1)` + `tryEmit`: input commands and ICE candidates are silently dropped
findings.evidence:
- `DeviceCommandChannel.kt:24` `MutableSharedFlow<CommandEnvelope>(replay = 1)` and `:73` `_commands.tryEmit(envelope)` (result ignored). The default overflow is SUSPEND, so a full buffer makes `tryEmit` return false.
  - The collector runs synchronously: `SessionController.kt:176` `collect { processCommand }`, and `processCommand` blocks on `su` (AR-06), so it typically holds 1 command and the buffer holds 1.
  - `PeerConnectionWrapper.kt:21,87` has the same pattern for local ICE candidates: `MutableSharedFlow<IceCandidate>(replay = 1)` with `_iceCandidates.tryEmit(candidate)`.
findings.scenario:
- Commands: while a tap blocks for about 1 s (each `input tap` starts a Dalvik VM, per the comment at `InputHandler.kt:~160`), one further command sits in the buffer and the next ones are dropped without an ack. A drag from the web UI (many SWIPE/KEY commands), or typing character by character, loses events. The browser's `sendCommandWithResponse` then times out.
  - ICE: libwebrtc emits several host, srflx and IPv6 candidates within milliseconds from a native thread. The Main-thread collector has not yet run, so all but one are dropped. A lost srflx candidate means no NAT traversal (works on LAN only because of peer-reflexive discovery from the browser side).
findings.fix: `MutableSharedFlow(replay = 0, extraBufferCapacity = 64, onBufferOverflow = DROP_OLDEST)` for ICE (or `Channel.UNLIMITED`), and a `Channel<CommandEnvelope>(capacity = 256)` for commands. Process on a dedicated single-thread dispatcher.

findings.title: Input is executed on the Main thread with `runBlocking` over `su` processes, no timeout; the video pipeline shares that thread
findings.evidence:
- `RemoteSessionService.kt:80` `serviceScope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main ...)`. This scope is passed to `SessionController` (`:298`), `RemoteSession` (`:~323`) and `VideoStreamBridge` (`SessionController.kt:208`).
  - `InputHandler.kt:74,98,124,217` use `runBlocking { injector.tap(...) }`, and `:201` does `Runtime.exec(arrayOf("su","0","sh","-c", shellCmd)).waitFor()` for MULTI_TAP on the same thread. `AdbShellInjector.kt:47` declares `COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000L`, but it is never used (`waitFor()` at `:133`).
findings.scenario:
- Every tap, swipe or key blocks the Main thread for about 100 ms to 1 s+, during which `VideoStreamBridge` (frame copy and chunking on Main) stalls and the video freezes while the operator interacts.
  - A first Magisk grant prompt, a hung su daemon, or `LongPress/Swipe durationMs=2000000` blocks Main indefinitely. That is an ANR and a frozen UI for the whole app, including the polling service's Main-bound pieces.
  - `MULTI_TAP count` is remote-controlled and unbounded (`CommandTypes.kt` `val count: Int = 3`): `count=500` starts 500 backgrounded `input` JVMs as root and can wedge the device.
findings.fix: run commands and video on `Dispatchers.IO`/a dedicated `newSingleThreadContext`, never `runBlocking`; use `withTimeout(COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS)` plus `process.destroyForcibly()`; clamp `durationMs` (to about 5 s), `count` (to about 10) and `intervalMs`. Better still, keep one persistent `su` shell (`sh` with stdin) or inject via a small persistent helper (the screen-server process already runs as shell/root and could expose `InputManager.injectInputEvent`) instead of paying a VM start per event.

findings.title: Remote desktop is root-only with no fallback, and capture failure is silent
findings.evidence:
- `RemoteSessionService.kt:102` `private var useScreenServer = true` (never changed), and `:203-208` the MediaProjection branch is dead.
  - `ScreenServerManager.kt:120-131` `isRooted()` only checks that an `su` file exists. `startViaShell()` (`:300-313`) runs `app_process` with the app's own uid, which has no SurfaceControl rights, so it can only fail.
  - `RemoteSessionService.kt:506-511`: when the screen server is not reachable after 5 tries, it logs and sets `isScreenCaptureActive = false`. Nothing is sent to the viewer, and `isAutoStartedSession` is already false so there is no retry.
  - `ScreenCaptureService.kt` is a TODO stub, and `ScreenCaptureManager`/`H264Encoder` are unreachable.
findings.scenario: on any device where `su` is missing, hidden, or the screen-server dies (the code itself notes Rockchip SurfaceControl failures), the viewer gets a connected session with no video and no explanation. The operator sees only a black panel. If `su` is missing, there is no way to get remote desktop at all, and it cannot be self-healed after a reboot on an adb-launched server.
findings.fix:
- Send a `CAPTURE_FAILED{reason}` ack/event over the data channel and surface it in the UI.
  - Retry capture with backoff while the session is up.
  - Auto-start the screen-server at boot on rooted devices (not only at session start), so the first START_REMOTE doesn't take about 4 s of su calls (`restartScreenServer` runs `ensureDeployed` + pkill + `startViaRoot` + `delay(1500)` each session).
  - Decide explicitly whether non-root devices are in scope. If they are, the only options are MediaProjection (human tap each time; not possible on a headless player) or the AccessibilityService screenshot API (API 30+, 1 fps class) as a degraded fallback.

findings.title: Screen-server abstract socket has no peer authentication: any app can read the screen
findings.evidence: `screen-server/Server.kt:56` `LocalServerSocket(params.socketName)` (abstract namespace `android-remote-video`) and `:62` `serverSocket.accept()` with no credential check; `ScreenServerClient.kt:91` connects with `LocalSocketAddress.Namespace.ABSTRACT`. Abstract sockets have no filesystem permissions.
findings.scenario: any installed app (such as the Footprints player itself, or anything sideloaded) connects to `@android-remote-video` and receives the live 1080p video of the whole screen (including secure content the device owner sees), with no user-visible indicator. Holding the single exclusive connection also blocks the legitimate client (the loop serves one client at a time), which is a trivial DoS against remote desktop.
findings.fix: use a filesystem socket under `/data/local/tmp` or the app's private dir with owner-only mode, or verify peer credentials (`LocalSocket.getPeerCredentials().uid`) against the app's uid passed with `-u <uid>`. A random per-session socket name (passed on the command line) is a cheap partial fix.

findings.title: A single bad command or ICE failure permanently kills the command/candidate collector
findings.evidence:
- `SessionController.kt:175-178` `scope.launch { commandChannel.commands.collect { processCommand(...) } }` has no try/catch per command.
  - `InputInjectionService.kt:84-88`: `GestureDescription.StrokeDescription(path, 0, spec.duration)` is built outside the `try` (the `try` starts at `:92`). It throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a duration over `GestureDescription.getMaxGestureDuration()` (60 s). SWIPE/LONG_PRESS/PINCH `durationMs` come straight from the wire and are only floor-clamped (`GestureBuilder.kt` `maxOf(durationMs, 50)`).
  - `RemoteSession.kt:197,221`: `client.iceCandidates.collect { pc.addIceCandidate(it) }` is unguarded, and `WebRtcPeerConnectionWrapper.kt` `addIceCandidate` throws `WebRtcException` on `onAddFailure`.
findings.scenario:
- A command with `durationMs=70000` (or any exception from a handler) terminates the collect. The `CoroutineExceptionHandler` just logs. The session stays `Connected` but every later command is ignored, with no acks and no error state, until a full reconnect.
  - ICE race: `startAsAnswerer` launches the offer handler and the remote-candidate collector as separate coroutines. A candidate that arrives right after the offer can reach `addIceCandidate` before `setRemoteDescription` completes, which fails ("no remote description"), the exception ends the collector, and every later candidate is lost.
findings.fix: wrap the body of each collect in `try/catch` and send a failure ack. Clamp durations (below 60 000 and above 0). Queue remote candidates until `setRemoteDescription` has completed, and `runCatching` each `addIceCandidate`.

findings.title: Boot auto-start passes the HTTP enrolment URL as the signaling URL; it always fails, then leaves a stuck "Screen is being shared" service
findings.evidence: `admin/BootReceiver.kt:~47-62` takes `sessionStorage.getServerUrl()` (an `http://host:port` string; see the ADB example in `MainActivity.kt:151-152`, `-e server_url "http://192.168.1.10:7899"`) and passes it as `EXTRA_SERVER_URL`. `KtorWebSocketProvider.kt` `WebSocketUrlParser.parse` throws `IllegalArgumentException("Invalid WebSocket URL scheme: http. Expected 'ws' or 'wss'")`. The path is `connect` -> `SignalingConnectionException` -> `handleConnectionError` -> `Error`. Meanwhile `RemoteSessionService.onStartCommand` has already called `startForeground` with the "Remote Control Active / Screen is being shared" notification and returns `START_STICKY`.
findings.scenario: every reboot of a device-owner device starts a foreground service that can never connect, and shows a permanent misleading notification on a kiosk screen. The service is also an extra process footprint on a boot that is already busy launching the kiosk app.
findings.fix: delete this auto-start (remote sessions are on-demand via START_REMOTE and boot already starts `CommandPollingService`), or convert to `ws(s)://.../ws` and don't call `startForeground` until a session actually starts.
