findings.title: Frame bigger than 1 MiB in ScreenServerClient ends the stream silently
findings.evidence: `ScreenServerClient.kt:159` `ByteArray(1024 * 1024)` and `:167-170` `if (size <= 0 || size > buffer.size) { Log.e(...); break }`. A `break` leaves `_isConnected = true` and does not call `reconnect()` or `onEarlyDeath`.
findings.scenario: the encoder runs at up to 8 Mbps with a 10 s keyframe interval (`SurfaceEncoder.kt:27`). A complex IDR at 1080p can exceed 1 MiB (an IDR of several hundred KB is routine). The reader coroutine then exits while the socket stays open. The server's `output.write` eventually blocks on a full socket, and the video is dead until the next START_REMOTE, with no signal to anyone.
findings.fix: allocate per-frame (`ByteArray(size)`, cap at about 8 MiB), and on protocol violation `disconnect()` and `reconnect()`.

findings.title: No flow control or loss handling on the video path (reliable, ordered, same channel as commands)
findings.evidence:
- `VideoStreamBridge.kt:~75` calls `videoChannel.sendFrame(...)` and ignores the Boolean result. `VideoChannel.kt:~90-108`: on a failed chunk it `break`s mid-frame, so a truncated frame is skipped.
  - `WebRtcDataChannel.kt:~27` `nativeChannel.send(buffer)` has no `bufferedAmount` check and `onBufferedAmountChange` is a no-op.
  - Video and commands use the same single `commands` channel (`RemoteSession.kt:~155`) with `ordered = true` (`useWebRTC.ts:~228`).
  - Defaults when the app starts the server: 1920 px, 8 Mbps, 60 fps (`Server.kt:97-102`); the only keyframe request mechanism, `H264Encoder.requestKeyFrame`, belongs to the unused path.
findings.scenario: a viewer on a 3-5 Mbps uplink gets 8 Mbps queued into the SCTP buffer: latency grows to many seconds, and the native buffer fills. When `send()` finally returns false, the partial frame is dropped, the decoder gets corrupt references, and nothing asks for an IDR, so artifacts last until the next keyframe (up to 10 s). Head-of-line blocking also delays acks and input echo on the shared channel.
findings.fix: check `bufferedAmount` (drop non-key frames above about 1 MB, and set a "need keyframe" flag so the next frame must be a keyframe); add a `REQUEST_KEYFRAME` message that makes the server call `MediaCodec.setParameters(PARAMETER_KEY_REQUEST_SYNC_FRAME)`; pass `-m 1280 -b 3000000 -f 30` from `startViaRoot`; consider a second unordered, `maxRetransmits=0` channel for video.

findings.title: No ICE TURN on the device; the browser's TURN is a shared public credential in the repo
findings.evidence: `RemoteSession.kt:46-52` `DEFAULT_CONFIG` has only `stun:stun.l.google.com:19302` and `stun1`, with the comment "TURN is disabled as it may cause stability issues". `RemoteSessionService.kt:~320` doesn't pass a `peerConnectionConfig`. The browser side (`web-ui/src/hooks/useWebRTC.ts:~108-121`) has the free metered "Open Relay" TURN with static username/credential committed in source.
findings.scenario: STUN only works for full-cone or restricted NAT. A device on mobile CGNAT or behind a symmetric NAT, with the viewer also behind a strict NAT, cannot connect (the browser's relay candidate helps only when the device's UDP is not blocked). The shared dev TURN may be rate limited or withdrawn without notice, and relaying customer screens through a third-party free server leaks content metadata.
findings.fix: run coturn (container) with time-limited credentials issued by the server (`/api/ice-config`), used by both sides; remove the committed credentials.

findings.title: Screen rotation and display changes are not handled (capture size and input mapping are fixed at start)
findings.evidence:
- `SurfaceEncoder.kt:58-67`: `capture.prepare()`, `writeHeader(size)` once (`headerWritten`), and the format is configured once. Nothing listens for rotation or `wm size` changes; `encodeLoop` runs until stopped.
  - `RemoteSessionService.kt:256-278`: `inputHandler.updateScreenConfig(...)` is called once in `onCreate`, and the grep shows no other call and no `onConfigurationChanged`.
findings.scenario: the player app switches orientation (or the service was created while the display was in another mode). The video keeps its old size and projection (content cropped or letterboxed), and taps map using the stale width/height/rotation, so the operator taps one place and the device clicks another. `CoordinateMapper` also inverts both axes at 180 degrees (`CoordinateMapper.kt:~64-69`) whereas the capture is rendered upright; I could not verify this on a device, treat as "check on hardware".
findings.fix: re-read `DisplayInfo` on a rotation callback (DisplayListener in the app, and a poll in the screen-server), restart the encoder loop with the new size and re-send the header; update the mapper on each START_REMOTE and on `DisplayListener.onDisplayChanged`.

findings.title: Re-sent START_REMOTE while connected leaves the new session without video (state-observer race)
findings.evidence: `RemoteSessionService.kt:184-195` sets `isAutoStartedSession = true` and launches `stateObserverJob`, which first receives the replayed current `StateFlow` value. At `:198` the condition `state is Connected && isAutoStartedSession && !isScreenCaptureActive` is true if the old session is still `Connected`, so it sets `isAutoStartedSession=false`, `isScreenCaptureActive=true` and starts `startScreenServerCapture()`. Then `connect()` (`SessionController.kt:87-90`) disconnects the old session. The started capture's `startVideoStream` finds `currentSession == null`, throws "No active session" (`:192`), and the catch at `RemoteSessionService.kt:435-439` returns. When the new session reaches `Connected`, the one-shot flag is already false, so capture is not started.
findings.scenario: the operator clicks "Remote" twice, or the UI re-issues START_REMOTE while a session is live (the `connect()` doc comment says this is an expected case). The new session connects, input works, and the video is black. `isScreenCaptureActive` and `isAutoStartedSession` are also plain `var`s touched from the Main and IO (`onEarlyDeath`, `:478-483`) threads with no volatile/synchronisation.
findings.fix: derive capture start from (`Connected`, `session identity`) instead of boolean flags (for example, key off a session counter incremented in `connect`), and mark the fields `@Volatile`/confine them to one dispatcher.

findings.title: Shell-injector probing blocks service creation on Main, and a failed probe is cached for the life of the process
findings.evidence: `RemoteSessionService.onCreate -> createSessionController` (`:118, :253, :286`) creates `InputHandler()`, whose `init` (`InputHandler.kt:29-37`) calls `isAvailable()`. `createSessionController` then calls `InputInjectorFactory.create()` and `isAvailable()` again, so this is done twice with separate injectors. `AdbShellInjector.isAvailable` (`:92-117`) runs up to four `Runtime.exec` + `waitFor()` calls (`su 0 id`, `su -c id`, `... input`) and caches the answer (`availabilityChecked = true`), including a negative one.
findings.scenario: `startForegroundService()` requires `startForeground` within about 5-10 s. If `su` is slow or shows a first-use grant prompt, `onCreate` blocks on Main and the process is killed (`ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException`). If the service is created early after boot before the su daemon is ready, `useRoot=false`, `input` runs without root, fails or does nothing for other apps, and `InputHandler.shellInjector` stays null, so all input falls back to an accessibility service that is not enabled ("Accessibility service not running") until the process restarts. (`Pinch`, `Scroll` and `MultiTap` never use the shell injector in the first place: `InputHandler.kt:138-165`.)
findings.fix: probe lazily on IO with a timeout; do not cache a negative result for more than a few seconds (or retry on each failure); reuse a single injector instance.

findings.title: Cleartext allow-list matches host names, not subnets
findings.evidence: `res/xml/network_security_config.xml:4-11` lists `<domain>192.168.0.0</domain>`, `192.168.1.0` and `192.168.68.0` under `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"`, with the comment "known local network ranges". A `<domain>` entry matches a host name, not a CIDR range. `base-config` forbids cleartext otherwise.
findings.scenario: a server reached by IP such as `http://192.168.68.20:7899` or `ws://192.168.68.20/ws` (which the ADB example in `MainActivity.kt:152` and the Postgres host in the owner's notes suggest) is not matched, so OkHttp refuses the connection with a "CLEARTEXT communication not permitted" error. This only works if the server is reached over HTTPS or by a listed hostname. I did not check what the deployed devices use.
findings.fix: terminate TLS on the server (preferred; signaling and the session token travel in clear today), or permit cleartext for the exact server host.

findings.title: Log/diagnostic hygiene on the input path
findings.evidence: `DeviceCommandChannel.kt:~76` `System.err.println("... Failed to deserialize command: ${e.message}, text=$text")` logs the full raw message, which can contain typed passwords from `TYPE_TEXT`. `AdbShellInjector.kt:~122` `Log.d(TAG, "Running: $command")` logs the text of every `input text` command.
findings.scenario: logcat (readable over adb, or via bug-report) contains credentials typed through the remote keyboard.
findings.fix: log only the length and type.

findings.title: Minor: screen-server shutdown hook accumulates; unused crypto
findings.evidence: `Server.kt:87-90` adds a new `Runtime.addShutdownHook(Thread { encoder.stop() })` for every client session in the accept loop, holding each old encoder alive. `RootDaemonBridge`/`CommandSigner` are used only by the placeholder `RootDaemonInjector`, and the factory returns null (`InputInjectorFactory.kt:~74`); `PairingStateMachine` has no caller in `app/src/main`.
findings.fix:
register the hook once, and either wire signing into AR-01 or drop the dead modules.

findings.title: Device-facing API calls carry no credential; server accepts them tokenless
findings.evidence: `api/CommandApiClient.kt:56` `httpClient.get("$baseUrl/api/devices/$deviceId/commands/pending")` (no header). Same for `TelemetryCollector.kt:109-112`, `CommandPollingService.kt:309` and `:747-750`. `grep Authorization|Bearer|x-session-token` over `app/src/main` returns nothing. The session token saved at enrollment (`MainActivity.kt:806`) is only used for the WebRTC session. Server: `server/src/app.ts:235-236` `if (!sessionToken) { return next(); // Allow without token for backward compat during migration`.
findings.scenario: anyone on the LAN who knows or guesses a device id (`device-xxxx`) can `GET /commands/pending`. The call marks the commands `delivered` (`commandStore.ts:154`), so the real device never receives its REBOOT/INSTALL_APK. They can also spoof telemetry, overwrite the app inventory (which feeds `app-updates`) and read `app-updates`. Because the token check is skipped when no token is sent, the "device session token" protection exists only on paper.
findings.fix: in `CommandApiClient`, the OkHttp telemetry/sync clients and the updates client, add `x-session-token` from `SessionStorage.getSessionToken()` (shared OkHttp interceptor). Then remove the "no token -> next()" branch on the server. Scope the ack by `deviceId` too (see AM-02).

findings.title: Command acknowledgements (PATCH) most likely hit the JWT gate and return 401, so no status ever reaches the server
findings.evidence: device ack is `PATCH /api/devices/{id}/commands/{cmdId}` (`CommandApiClient.kt:132-134`). Server gate: `server/src/app.ts:222` `deviceFacingPaths = ['/heartbeat','/telemetry','/apps','/commands/pending','/events']`, and the PATCH route is `app.ts:1239`. `path.includes(...)` matches none of those for `/devices/<id>/commands/<uuid>`, so the request falls through to `authMiddleware` (`middleware/auth.ts:46-49`), which needs `Authorization: Bearer <admin JWT>`. The device sends none. The server tests probably do not cover this because they run without the gate or with a JWT (not checked).
findings.scenario: the device executes INSTALL_APK, REBOOT, etc. and `markExecuting`/`markCompleted`/`markFailed` get a 401. `acknowledgeCommand` treats 401 as `false` and does not retry (`CommandApiClient.kt:151-154`). In the UI every command stays "delivered" forever and install failures (owner need 2) are never reported back. I did not run it; confirm with `curl -X PATCH` from an unauthenticated client.
findings.fix: add `/commands/` PATCH to the device-facing rules (match `^/devices/[^/]+/commands/[^/]+$` for PATCH) and require the session token. In `acknowledgeCommand` also require `device_id = ?` so one device cannot ack another's command (today only `cmdId` is used, `commandStore.ts:195-206`).

findings.title: One stuck command freezes the entire polling loop (no timeout on install/uninstall callbacks)
findings.evidence: commands run sequentially inside the loop (`CommandPollingService.kt:243-263`, `360-362`). `SilentPackageInstaller.installSilently` (`:197-298`) waits on `suspendCancellableCoroutine` with no `withTimeout`. `InstallResultReceiver.kt:94-115` on `STATUS_PENDING_USER_ACTION` logs "Cannot launch confirmation intent from receiver" and returns without invoking the callback ("wait for actual result"). The same applies if the system never sends a result.
findings.scenario: a silent install that needs confirmation (for example an update of an app whose installer of record differs, a package-verifier prompt, or the OEM showing a dialog) never completes. The poll coroutine suspends forever, so REBOOT, LOCK, telemetry and every later command are dead until the process is killed. Device shows online in the UI only if something else updates last-seen. Same for `checkAndInstallAppUpdates` (`:334`), which also runs inside the loop.
findings.fix: wrap each install/uninstall in `withTimeout(5.minutes)`, abandon the session on timeout, and report failure. For `PENDING_USER_ACTION` resume the callback with `Failure` (DO installs should not prompt) or launch the confirm intent from a context that can. Consider running slow commands in a child coroutine (with a `Mutex` for installs) so REBOOT/LOCK are not blocked behind a large download.

findings.title: At-most-once command delivery: crash or lost response silently drops commands; ack result is ignored
findings.evidence: server marks `delivered` as soon as it returns the list (`commandStore.ts:147-156`) and `getPendingCommands` only selects `status='pending'`. No requeue or stale-`delivered` sweep exists (grep for stale/requeue in `server/src` finds only WebSocket cleanup). Device: `CommandPollingService.kt:374` `client.markExecuting(command.id)` ignores the Boolean result, then runs the command anyway. REBOOT (`:379`) and WIPE return after the device is already going down, so `completed` is never sent. Self-update (`:447-455`) kills the process mid-command.
findings.scenario: (a) response lost on flaky Wi-Fi after the server flipped to `delivered`: the command is lost with no trace. (b) The service is killed between fetch and execute (self-update, OOM, user swipe): the second and later commands in the batch are lost. (c) Reboot/self-update commands stay `executing` forever. Duplicate execution is not a problem today (good), but loss is.
findings.fix: on the server, requeue `delivered`/`executing` commands older than N minutes that are idempotent (INSTALL_APK, SYNC_*), and never requeue WIPE/REBOOT. On the device, persist "last command id + status" in SharedPreferences before executing. For REBOOT, send `completed` first and then reboot. After a self-update, the new process should report `completed` for the pending self-update command in `PackageUpdateReceiver`.

findings.title: APK install has no integrity or provenance check; accepts any URL, including cleartext
findings.evidence: `SilentPackageInstaller.kt:153-195` `URL(url).openConnection()` with no hash, no signature/cert check, no size check. `CommandPollingService.kt:438-443` takes `urlPath` from the payload as-is when it is not relative. `:326-330` does the same for `app-updates` entries. Only mitigation found: `params.setAppPackageName(packageName)` (`SilentPackageInstaller.kt:206`) makes the platform reject a mismatched package name, and Android enforces same-signature on updates of an installed package. A brand-new package name has no such protection.
findings.scenario: the installer runs as Device Owner, so it installs silently. Anyone who can alter the download (MITM on a cleartext LAN leg, a compromised file host, a poisoned `apkUrl`, the unauthenticated polling API in AM-01) can push an arbitrary new APK with any package name and, if it is also on the boot list, have it auto-started. The server stores `versionCode` but no digest, and the payload carries none.
findings.fix: put `sha256` (and expected `versionCode`) in the INSTALL_APK payload and in `app-updates` entries (server computes it at upload). Hash while downloading and refuse on mismatch. Require `https://` or the enrolled server's origin. Optionally pin an allowed signer cert SHA-256 per package and check `PackageManager.getPackageArchiveInfo(..., GET_SIGNING_CERTIFICATES)` before opening the session.

findings.title: Cleartext allow-list in network security config does not match LAN IPs
findings.evidence: `res/xml/network_security_config.xml` lists `<domain includeSubdomains="true">192.168.68.0</domain>` (also 192.168.0.0, 192.168.1.0). `domain` entries match host names or exact IP literals; they are not CIDR ranges. The default server is `buildConfigField ... "http://192.168.68.209:7899"` (`build.gradle.kts:20`) and the documented ADB example is `http://192.168.1.10:7899` (`MainActivity.kt:152`). `base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"`.
findings.scenario: the comment says "LAN-only cleartext", but a device at 192.168.68.209 gets `Cleartext HTTP traffic to 192.168.68.209 not permitted`. Either every deployment is already using HTTPS or a hostname that happens to match (then the file is dead config), or enrollment against the default URL fails. I did not test on a device. The file also gives false assurance that only LAN cleartext is possible. `MainActivity.kt:240` also builds `http://` for any port except 443 and accepts any address.
findings.fix: decide the deployment. Prefer HTTPS everywhere and set `cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"` with no exception. If LAN HTTP is required, list the real server host/IP only. Add a debug-only config for 10.0.2.2/localhost. If the server uses a private CA, add `<certificates src="@raw/ca"/>` and optionally `<pin-set>`.

findings.title: "Start one app on boot / keep it in front" is only a one-shot BOOT_COMPLETED launch; no kiosk, no relaunch
findings.evidence: boot list is the `boot_apps` SharedPreferences (`CommandPollingService.kt:489-507`), read once by `mdm/BootReceiver.kt:41-73`. Launch is `Thread.sleep(8000)` then `startActivity(...)` (`:58-66`, `:176-184`). `CommandPollingService.kt:834-835` `// TODO: Apply kiosk mode (lock task mode) if enabled`. `grep setLockTaskPackages|startLockTask|PersistentPreferredActivity|LOCKED_BOOT` finds nothing. `kiosk_mode` is stored (`:778`) and never read.
findings.scenario: the Footprints player crashes, the user presses Home, a dialog covers it, or the player is auto-updated: nothing brings it back until the next reboot. No HOME replacement means the OEM launcher stays reachable. Android version notes (minSdk 30, targetSdk 35, so N-era checks are dead code): `BOOT_COMPLETED` arrives only after the first user unlock, so on a device with a lock screen PIN the player does not start after a power cut until someone unlocks. There is no `LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED`/direct-boot handling. Background activity start from a receiver/service is restricted on Android 10+ (DO apps are exempt in most builds, but I have not verified this on the target devices; there is no SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW fallback).
findings.fix: `dpm.setLockTaskPackages(admin, arrayOf(playerPkg, ownPkg))` and `startLockTask()` from a small trampoline activity, or `addPersistentPreferredActivity(admin, homeFilter, playerComponent)` so the player is HOME. Add a watchdog in the polling service (every poll: if `foregroundApp` is set and its process/top activity is not up, relaunch) and a `ACTION_PACKAGE_REPLACED`/`PACKAGE_ADDED` receiver for the target package. Use `dpm.setKeyguardDisabled`/no lock screen for signage devices.

findings.title: Auto-update installs any newer package at any time and never relaunches the target app
findings.evidence: `CommandPollingService.kt:250-254` runs `checkAndInstallAppUpdates()` every 6th poll. The loop `:325-339` installs each update and only logs the result. There is no `launchApp` call, unlike the command path at `:468-471`. No maintenance window, no per-app opt-out, and no battery or charging check.
findings.scenario: the server gets a new player APK. Within a minute every device installs it. Package replace force-stops the running player and nothing restarts it (see AM-07). All screens go dark mid-day until reboot. Combined with AM-05, a bad upload bricks the fleet. If the update install fails, it is retried every ~60 s forever (full re-download each time, AM-13).
findings.fix: after a successful update of a package in `boot_apps`, relaunch it (`launchAppWithRetry`). Add a per-device update window and "staged rollout" flag on the server, and back off failed updates (store last failure per package+versionCode, retry after 1 h/6 h/24 h).

findings.title: Boot/foreground preferences can only be added, never removed; SYNC_POLICY resets silent mode on missing fields
findings.evidence: `executeSyncPolicy` only calls `saveBootStartApp` for apps present in `requiredApps` (`CommandPollingService.kt:816-820`); nothing deletes a `boot_apps` entry when an app is removed from policy or uninstalled (`executeUninstallApp` `:550-559` does not touch `boot_apps`). `saveBootStartApp` clears the old foreground only when a new foreground is set (`:493-500`). `:772` `silentMode = payload["silentMode"]... ?: false`, so a payload without the field disables silent mode. `:773` same for kiosk.
findings.scenario: admin switches the foreground app from A to B in the policy; A is still launched as a regular boot app after every reboot. Admin removes A from the policy and A still starts. An uninstalled package yields 3 failed launch attempts + 2 s sleeps at every boot (`mdm/BootReceiver.kt:151-201`).
findings.fix: treat SYNC_POLICY as authoritative: rebuild `boot_apps` from `requiredApps` in one `edit().clear()...apply()`. Remove the entry on uninstall. Use `null`-aware parsing for silent/kiosk so absent means "unchanged".

findings.title: Boot path: two BOOT_COMPLETED receivers, unguarded foreground-service start, order undefined
findings.evidence: manifest registers both `.mdm.BootReceiver` and `.admin.BootReceiver` for BOOT_COMPLETED (`AndroidManifest.xml:139-155`). `admin/BootReceiver.kt:63` `context.startForegroundService(serviceIntent)` for `RemoteSessionService`, which is declared `foregroundServiceType="mediaProjection|specialUse"` (manifest `:83`) and calls `startForeground(NOTIFICATION_ID, notification)` with no type (`RemoteSessionService.kt:172`). No try/catch in the receiver. `mdm/BootReceiver` starts `MainActivity` and relies on it to start polling (`MainActivity.kt:622-629`), while `admin/BootReceiver.kt:48` starts polling directly with `5000L`.
findings.scenario: on Android 14/15 (targetSdk 35) a mediaProjection FGS requires an existing projection grant and Android 15 forbids starting it from BOOT_COMPLETED. The call throws (`ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`/`SecurityException`) inside `onReceive`, which crashes the process on every boot. Polling was started first, but the crash can kill that fresh service or leave it to START_STICKY recovery. I have not reproduced this on a device; confirm on an Android 15 unit. Separately, `onStartCommand` re-runs `initializeAndStartPolling()` on each of the up to three start calls (boot x2 + MainActivity), creating a new `CommandApiClient` each time and leaking the previous one (`:191`) and re-sending initial telemetry.
findings.fix: keep one boot receiver that only starts `CommandPollingService`. Start `RemoteSessionService` lazily on the START_REMOTE command, never from boot. Wrap FGS starts in try/catch. Make `initializeAndStartPolling` idempotent (return if `isPolling`).

findings.title: Poll loop survival: no wake/wifi lock, battery-optimization exemption is a stub, plain `delay` loop
findings.evidence: `DeviceOwnerManager.kt:282-304` `exemptFromBatteryOptimization()` for a Device Owner just logs and `return true` ("The app should already be exempt ... for most manufacturers"). It does nothing. `grep WakeLock|WifiLock|WorkManager|AlarmManager` finds no usage in `app/src/main`. The loop is `while (isActive && isPolling) { ... delay(pollIntervalMs) }` (`CommandPollingService.kt:244-263`). `pollIntervalMs` is clamped to a 10 s minimum (`:149`) so the `5000L` passed by every caller (`MainActivity.kt:361,629,812`, both boot receivers) silently becomes 10 s; the comment at `:114` ("6 polls = 30 seconds with 5s interval") is wrong (actual telemetry period: 60 s).
findings.scenario: for a plugged-in signage player with the screen on this is fine. For a device whose screen is off or idle (Doze: network suspended, timers deferred to maintenance windows) commands, including REBOOT, arrive minutes to hours late. Manual Settings exemption is prompted in the UI (`MainActivity.kt:595` reads `batteryOptDisabled`), so this is mitigated only if an operator completes it on every device.
findings.fix: for DO devices use a documented route (e.g. `dpm.setPermittedInputMethods` is irrelevant here; use `adb shell dumpsys deviceidle whitelist +com.androidremote.app` at provisioning, or `ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` once, and `setUserControlDisabledPackages` on API 30+ to stop users force-stopping the agent). Take a partial `WifiLock` while polling. Add an FCM/long-poll or WebSocket push wake-up if sub-10 s latency is needed. Remove the misleading stub or make it return false.

findings.title: No backoff on errors; a 404 or outage keeps the loop at full rate
findings.evidence: `CommandPollingService.kt:255-262` logs and falls through to the same `delay(pollIntervalMs)` for every exception, including `DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` (device deleted on server). No jitter. Each failure logs a full stack (`Log.e(TAG, "Unexpected error during polling", e)`).
findings.scenario: server down for an hour with 500 devices: 500 requests every 10 s as soon as it returns (thundering herd); a deleted device polls forever. The loop itself does survive exceptions (good), but the `try` also wraps `sendPeriodicTelemetry`/`checkAndInstallAppUpdates`, so a slow install delays command polling (AM-03).
findings.fix: exponential backoff with jitter (10 s -> 5 min) on consecutive failures, reset on success, and stop or slow to 5 min on 404.

findings.title: Download path is fragile for large APKs and flaky networks
findings.evidence: `SilentPackageInstaller.kt:153-195`: `readTimeout = 60_000` is per read, no overall deadline, no `Range` resume, no free-space check, ignores `contentLength` vs bytes written. `tempFile` is created inside `downloadApk` and only deleted in the `finally` that wraps `installFromFile` (`:61-69`), so an `IOException` during the copy leaves a partial file in `cacheDir`. `installSilently` writes the APK a second time into the session (2x disk). On exception after `createSession` (`:208`) the session is never abandoned (`catch` at `:287` does not call `abandon`), and the registered callback is not removed. `checkAndInstallAppUpdates` builds a new `HttpClient(OkHttp)` per call and does not close it if `get`/`body` throws (`:303-310`).
findings.scenario: 150 MB player APK over weak Wi-Fi: the transfer drops at 90 MB, restarts from zero on the next 60 s cycle, leaves 90 MB of garbage each time (cache fills, installs start failing with `STATUS_FAILURE_STORAGE`), and orphan sessions accumulate (Android caps open sessions per app).
findings.fix: download to `filesDir/apk_staging/<pkg>.part` with `Range` resume and `If-Range`, verify length + sha256 (AM-05), then stream straight into the session. `abandon()` the session and `unregisterCallback` in the failure path. Delete stale `.part` files at service start. Check `StatFs` before starting.

findings.title: Exported launcher activity accepts enrollment token and server URL from any app
findings.evidence: `AndroidManifest.xml:63-71` `MainActivity android:exported="true"`. `MainActivity.kt:160-185` reads `enrollment_token` and `server_url` extras and, if not yet enrolled, saves the URL and calls `startEnrollment(token)`. The ADB comment at `:151-153` shows the intended use.
findings.scenario: on a provisioned-but-not-yet-enrolled device (the window between `dpm set-device-owner` and enrollment), any installed app can fire `startActivity` with an attacker `server_url` and a token it controls. The device then enrolls to the attacker's server, which has Device Owner command power (silent install, wipe). After enrollment the path is blocked (`isEnrolled()` check).
findings.fix: only honour the extras when `BuildConfig.DEBUG` or when the caller is the shell (`Binder.getCallingUid() == 2000`, which is not available to activities, so instead use `getReferrer()`/`callingActivity`), or provision via the DPC admin-extras bundle (`onProfileProvisioningComplete`/`EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE`). At minimum require `https://` and show a confirmation.

findings.title: Device identity and fallback token can leave the device through backup; secure store silently degrades to plaintext
findings.evidence: `AndroidManifest.xml:52` `android:allowBackup="true"`. `res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml:14-17` and `:30-33` include `enrollment_prefs.xml` (device id, server URL, enrolled flag) and `session_prefs_fallback.xml`. `ui/SessionStorage.kt:66-70`: any exception creating `EncryptedSharedPreferences` falls back to a plain prefs file named `session_prefs_fallback`, which is exactly what the backup rules include. Device id and URL are also kept outside encryption on purpose (`:13-18`).
findings.scenario: (a) if the Keystore is unavailable, the session token is stored in cleartext and then uploaded to Google backup / copied by device-transfer. (b) A restored or transferred device inherits another device's `device_id` + `enrolled=true`, so it polls as the original device (and, given AM-01, needs no secret to do so). Two physical players then share one id and steal each other's commands.
findings.fix: `allowBackup="false"`, or exclude all three prefs files. Do not fall back to plaintext: fail closed and re-enroll. Use the Keystore-backed AEAD directly (androidx.security-crypto is deprecated).

findings.title: Wipe and uninstall have no safeguards
findings.evidence: `CommandPollingService.kt:583-600` `executeWipe`: only `isDeviceOwner()`, then `wipeDevice(flags)` with `WIPE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` by default (`keepData` absent -> false). No second factor, delay, allow-list or "enabled" setting. `:550-559` `executeUninstallApp` accepts any `packageName`, including `com.androidremote.app` (removing the agent and, once DO is cleared, the control channel) or the system settings/packages. The same wipe/reboot/lock is also reachable over the WebRTC data channel via `controller/MdmHandler.kt:102-122` (`SessionController.kt:397-403`); that path's authentication belongs to the media-path reviewer.
findings.scenario: an unauthenticated or mis-authorised command (AM-01 does not allow queueing, but a compromised admin session or a script bug with `type=WIPE` does) factory-resets a fleet with no recovery. A mis-typed `UNINSTALL_APP` for the agent bricks remote management.
findings.fix: refuse uninstall of own package and of a configured protected list. Make WIPE require a one-time confirmation code or a `wipeEnabled` device setting, a `requestedBy`/`reason` field in the payload, and record an audit event before executing. Do not default to wiping external storage.

findings.title: App management is limited to install/uninstall; disable, permissions and launch are missing
findings.evidence: the command switch (`CommandPollingService.kt:377-391`) has INSTALL_APK, UNINSTALL_APP, LOCK, REBOOT, WIPE, START_REMOTE, TAKE_SCREENSHOT (always fails, `:633-638`), GET_LOCATION, REFRESH_TELEMETRY, SYNC_APPS, SYNC_POLICY, SET_VOLUME. `DeviceOwnerManager.grantPermission/revokePermission` (`:116-163`) only act on `context.packageName`. `grep setApplicationHidden|setPackagesSuspended` finds only a comment. `executeSyncApps` reports an `enabled` flag (`:724`) that nothing can change. `CommandType` enum in `api/CommandModels.kt:9-16` lists only six types and does not match the handler.
findings.scenario: the owner cannot disable a bundled app, grant the player its camera/storage/overlay permissions remotely, clear a corrupted app's data, force-stop/launch an app, or start/stop the player on demand (the only launch paths are install flags and the boot list).
findings.fix: add `SET_APP_STATE` (`setApplicationHidden`/`setPackagesSuspended`), `SET_PERMISSION` (`setPermissionGrantState(admin, pkg, perm, state)` for any package), `CLEAR_APP_DATA` (`clearApplicationUserData`), `LAUNCH_APP`/`STOP_APP`. Align `CommandType` with the handler and reject unknown types explicitly on the server too.

findings.title: Telemetry: snapshot only, no offline buffering, ignores the server's report interval
findings.evidence: `TelemetryCollector.sendTelemetry` (`:101-132`) collects and POSTs one snapshot and returns `false` on any failure; nothing is queued. Callers: every 6th poll (`CommandPollingService.kt:250-253`, 60 s at the effective 10 s interval). The server answers `nextReportIn: 60000` (`app.ts:1357`) which the client ignores. Payload fields (`TelemetryData`, `:310-329`): battery, network type/SSID/IP/RSSI, storage, memory, screen on, brightness, location, uptime, security patch.
findings.scenario: for owner analytics (is the player running, was it up yesterday, how long was it offline) the data is too thin and lossy. Nothing records which app is in the foreground, whether the player process is alive, its version, last crash, reboot count, or display state. A 2 h Wi-Fi outage leaves a 2 h hole with no way to backfill. Cost is small (about 1 KB/min, plus a poll every 10 s), but the work runs inside the poll coroutine (AM-03) with blocking OkHttp calls.
findings.fix: write samples to a small Room/file ring buffer with timestamps, flush batches (e.g. 15 min or on reconnect) as `POST /telemetry/batch`, add `foregroundPackage`, `playerVersionCode`, `playerRunning`, `lastBootTime`. Honour `nextReportIn`. Run telemetry on its own coroutine.

findings.title: Location in telemetry is cached forever and effectively always null
findings.evidence: `TelemetryCollector.kt:249-253` `private var cachedLocation ... if (cachedLocation != null) return cachedLocation` with no expiry; one instance lives for the life of the service (`CommandPollingService.kt:128`). `DeviceOwnerManager.kt:44-53` deliberately does not grant location, and `MainActivity.kt:144` calls `revokeLocationPermissions()`. `getIpAddress` (`:188-195`) uses the Wi-Fi manager only, so Ethernet devices report null.
findings.scenario: the first fix (if ever granted) is reported forever, even after the device is moved. By default the location fields are always empty, and GET_LOCATION (`:640-690`) fails with "Location permission not granted" while still saying "Ensure GPS is enabled".
findings.fix: drop the cache or give it a 10 min TTL. Decide whether location is wanted; if not, remove the fields and command. Report Ethernet addresses via `LinkProperties`.

findings.title: Hand-built JSON in app inventory sync breaks on backslashes and control characters
findings.evidence: `CommandPollingService.kt:718-742` builds JSON by string concatenation, escaping only `"` (`.replace("\"", "\\\"")`) for `appName` and `versionName`.
findings.scenario: an app label containing `\`, a newline or a tab produces invalid JSON; the server rejects the whole inventory and the device shows no apps (and `app-updates` stops working for it).
findings.fix: build with `kotlinx.serialization` (`buildJsonObject`) which is already a dependency.

findings.title: Non-Device-Owner install path is broken and reports success
findings.evidence: `SilentPackageInstaller.kt:301-325` `Uri.fromFile(file)` with `ACTION_VIEW` (throws `FileUriExposedException` on API 24+, caught as a failure), and even if it worked, `installFromUrl` deletes the file in `finally` immediately (`:61-69`). On the success side `CommandPollingService.kt:475-481` maps `UserPromptShown` to `CommandResult.success()`.
findings.scenario: on a device that lost Device Owner (or the admin-only fallback), INSTALL_APK fails with an odd error or "succeeds" without installing anything.
findings.fix: for non-DO, either fail explicitly ("requires Device Owner") or use a `PackageInstaller` session with `USER_ACTION_REQUIRED` and a `FileProvider`. Report `UserPromptShown` as a distinct status, not `completed`.

findings.title: Build and manifest hygiene
findings.evidence:
- `app/build.gradle.kts:15` `versionCode = 1` is constant, so the server's versionCode comparison (`app.ts:1820+`) cannot detect a new agent build (self-update via `app-updates` never triggers; only the manual INSTALL_APK path works).
  - `app/build.gradle.kts:70` copies `screen-server-debug.apk` into assets for all variants, so release builds ship a debug-signed, unobfuscated helper that the app runs with root (`ScreenServerManager`, not reviewed).
  - `AndroidManifest.xml:21` `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` and `:36` `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` are declared; `feature-files` (SAFFileService) is built into the app (`build.gradle.kts:87`) but not referenced anywhere in `app/src/main`, so the owner has no remote file feature and the broad permission buys nothing.
  - HEAD references a non-existent `AdminNotificationManager` (only fixed by the uncommitted diff), so a clean checkout of master does not build.
  - No release `signingConfig`; `debuggable` is not set (default false for release, good), minify is on.
findings.fix: derive `versionCode` from CI/git count; bundle the release screen-server; drop unused permissions; commit the diff.

findings.title: Secrets and identifiers in logs
findings.evidence: `MainActivity.kt:169` `Log.i(TAG, "ADB auto-enrollment: token=$token, serverUrl=$serverUrl")` (enrollment token); `ui/SessionStorage.kt:149,160` log device id and server URL on every read (the poll loop reads them constantly); `CommandApiClient.kt:54` logs the device id each poll.
findings.scenario: on Android 11+ other apps cannot read logcat, but `adb logcat`/bug reports from the field contain a still-valid enrollment token and device ids.
findings.fix: drop the token from the log line and remove the per-read debug logs (or guard with `BuildConfig.DEBUG`).

findings.title: Silent mode: the secure-settings write cannot work for a DO and clobbers the list
findings.evidence: `DeviceOwnerManager.kt:328-332` `Settings.Secure.putString(..., "enabled_notification_policy_access_packages", context.packageName)`. This needs `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` (not declared, not grantable to a DO via `setPermissionGrantState`), and would overwrite the whole list. It is caught and logged at debug (`:334-336`).
findings.scenario: DND stays unavailable; "silent mode" depends on the audio-stream mute and `setMasterVolumeMuted`, which Android may reset when volume keys are pressed.
findings.fix: use `dpm.setSecureSetting`/`setGlobalSetting` only for allowed keys, or grant DND access once at provisioning via `adb shell cmd notification allow_dnd com.androidremote.app`.

well.server-security.md:
- No SQL injection found: every value goes through better-sqlite3 `?` binding; dynamic SQL is only placeholder lists and a fixed-column SET list.
- Admin JWT uses `jwt.verify` with a server-held secret, bcrypt (cost 12) for the password, and production refuses to start without JWT_SECRET (index.ts:9-13).
- Command enqueue (`/api/commands`, `/api/devices/:id/commands`, `/commands/batch`) is behind JWT: an unauthenticated party cannot enqueue REBOOT/WIPE/RUN_SHELL/INSTALL_APK directly (the takeover paths above go through enrollment/pairing/WS instead). Command type is whitelisted against COMMAND_TYPES and the DB has a CHECK constraint.
- Device-token check, when a token is supplied, is bound to the path device id and honours expiry (validateSessionToken); session tokens are 32 random bytes, enrollment tokens use `crypto.randomBytes`.
- Installer download requires an active enrollment token and is rate limited; agent upload/binaries listing require JWT; uploads are size-capped (500 MB APK, 200 MB binaries); helmet is on; production error handler hides stack traces.
- Tests: server/test covers pairing/enrollment/commands/signaling happy paths but contains no authorization tests (nothing asserts that `/api/enroll/tokens`, `/ws`, or `/admin` reject anonymous callers), which is why SS-01/02/05 went unnoticed.
well.server-reliability.md:
- WAL + `foreign_keys=ON` set (`db/connection.ts:25-28`); better-sqlite3 default 5 s busy timeout applies; single process, synchronous API, so `getPendingCommands` has no inter-request race.
- Partial index `idx_device_commands_pending (device_id, status) WHERE status='pending'` matches the poll query exactly; `device_events`/`telemetry_history` have `(device_id, time DESC)` indexes; `syncDeviceApps` is in a `db.transaction` (`appInventoryStore.ts:119-122`).
- Command acks are forward-only (`WHERE status IN (...)`), so duplicate/late acks are idempotent and cannot resurrect a completed command; `cancelCommand` only deletes `pending`.
- Event listener errors are isolated (`eventStore.ts:130-136`); agent heartbeat loop and stale-agent sweep exist for the relay and clean up viewer sessions on agent loss (`agentConnectionStore.removeAgent`); relay auth has a 10 s timeout and cleans timers on close.
- Production refuses to start without `JWT_SECRET` (`index.ts:13-16`); error middleware hides internals in production (`app.ts:2815`); CORS callback does not turn into 500s.
- Android side retries ack with backoff and keeps polling after errors, so server-side fixes above (SR-01/02/03) will take effect without protocol changes.
well.web-ui.md:
- No HTML injection sinks: no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`innerHTML`; device strings are rendered as React text.
- CSP meta tag is present with `default-src 'self'`, so inline/injected scripts are blocked; no external script or CDN dependencies in `index.html`.
- Central `apiFetch` handles 401 by clearing the token and redirecting; `ProtectedRoute` plus `mustChangePassword` redirect is correct; token validated on mount (`/api/auth/verify`).
- VideoFrames are always `close()`d in `renderFrame`; `ImageBitmap`s are closed in `renderTile`; decoder is closed in `destroy()`. No frame-memory leak found.
- Chunk reassembly has a staleness GC; SPS parser handles high-profile scaling lists and cropping; keyframes get cached SPS/PPS prepended.
- Unenroll, group/policy delete and deploy-to-all do have confirm dialogs; device command history polls only while a command is in flight (useCommands.ts:104-114).
- Android canvas dimensions follow the decoded frame size on rotation (renderFrame updates `canvas.width/height` and notifies the parent).
well.android-remote.md:
- The screen-server is a proper scrcpy-style design. It falls back from DisplayManager to SurfaceControl, retries with physical size and smaller max sizes (`prepareRetry`), has a first-frame timeout so a stuck SurfaceControl cannot hang the accept loop (`SurfaceEncoder.kt:162-168`), and releases codec, surface and display in `finally` (`:100-118`). The app also restarts the server per session (`restartScreenServer`), which sidesteps a stuck encoder.
- The start order is right: the video bridge subscribes before the screen-server connects, so the first SPS/PPS and IDR are not lost (`RemoteSessionService.kt:428-439`). The native-teardown ordering is careful (`closeSync` before `PeerConnectionFactory.dispose`, comments on the SIGSEGV).
- `ScreenServerClient` has a connect-time header timeout (5 s) and early-death detection.
- `VideoChannel` chunking is simple, with a documented framing, and `CoordinateMapper` clamps its inputs; `DeviceCommandChannel.onMessage` catches decode errors so malformed JSON can't crash the app (the problem is what valid JSON may do, AR-01, 02, 06, 09).
- Binary frames are not interpreted as commands (`onMessage(data: ByteArray)` is a no-op), and `core-crypto`'s primitives are sound (Ed25519/X25519 via BouncyCastle, HKDF-SHA256, HMAC-SHA256, constant-time compare, `SecureRandom`, no hard-coded keys or IVs). They are simply not on the live path.
well.android-mdm.md:
- Command execution is deduplicated by design: the server flips `pending` to `delivered` in the same call, and the device marks `executing` before running, so a REBOOT or WIPE cannot run twice in a loop.
- The poll loop catches every exception per iteration, and each command is wrapped so a failure is reported instead of killing the loop. Reporting failures are in their own try/catch.
- Ack calls retry 3 times with 2 s/4 s backoff on exceptions.
- `setAppPackageName` plus platform signature rules protect against package-name swaps on updates; the `PendingIntent` for installer results is explicit-component and not exported.
- `PackageUpdateReceiver` and the self-update pre-save (`:447-451`) show real thought about the agent updating itself.
- Silent install uses the proper `PackageInstaller` session API with `fsync` and result callbacks; uninstall is also silent for a DO.
- Manifest hygiene is decent: components not exported by default, proper FGS permissions and type, `specialUse` subtype declared, release minify enabled, base config blocks cleartext and user CAs.
- Telemetry collection isolates each metric with `safeCall`, so one failing sensor does not drop the report.

trace:
1. Reboot: `CommandPollingService.executeReboot` -> `DeviceOwnerManager.rebootDevice()` -> `DevicePolicyManager.reboot(admin)`. Device Owner only, correct API, minSdk 30 so version check is moot. The command is never marked completed (AM-04) and the ack route likely 401s (AM-02).
2. App install: server URL from payload -> `HttpURLConnection` -> temp file -> `PackageInstaller` session -> `InstallResultReceiver` callback. No hash/signature check (AM-05), no timeout (AM-03), fragile on large APKs (AM-13). Failures are reported via `markFailed` with the message from the installer, but the PATCH likely never lands (AM-02).
3. Boot app: SharedPreferences list + `BOOT_COMPLETED` + 8 s sleep + `startActivity`. No lock task, no HOME, no watchdog, no relaunch after update/crash (AM-07, AM-08, AM-09, AM-10).
4. Manage apps: uninstall works (no protection list, AM-16). No disable, no per-app permissions (AM-17). Inventory sync works but is fragile (AM-20).
5. Telemetry: 18 fields every ~60 s, no buffering (AM-18, AM-19).
6. Polling service: foreground service of type `specialUse` (property declared, good) plus `START_STICKY`, coroutine `while` loop on `Dispatchers.IO` with a `SupervisorJob`; restarts after reboot via the boot receivers and after self-update via `PackageUpdateReceiver` (`MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED`). Exceptions inside the loop are caught, so it does not die silently. Weaknesses: AM-03, AM-10, AM-11, AM-12.

On-device security checklist: exported components are minimal (only `MainActivity` and `DeviceOwnerReceiver`, which is protected by `BIND_DEVICE_ADMIN`; the accessibility service has `BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE`; all other receivers/services `exported=false`). No shell exec is reachable from polled server commands (the `Runtime.exec` calls are in the remote-input and screen-server code paths: `InputHandler.kt:200` builds its command from integers only). Not debuggable in release. Server URL and device id are stored unencrypted by design; the token is encrypted with a plaintext fallback (AM-15). No certificate pinning, system CAs only (acceptable for a LAN CA, see AM-06).
